1.   Le Gouvernement de la République Démocratique du Congo (« l’Emprunteur ») a obtenu un crédit et un don de la Banque mondiale pour financer le coût du Projet d'Accès, de Gouvernance et de Réforme des secteurs de l'Electricité et de l'Eau (AGREE). Il est prévu qu’une partie des sommes accordées au titre de ce financement sera utilisée pour effectuer les paiements prévus au titre du marché de Conception, la fourniture et l’installation d’un Système Intégré d’Information de Gestion supporté par un Système d’Information Géographique (SIG – SIG) pour la Société Nationale d’Électricité (SNEL SA).

Pour ce Marché, l’Emprunteur effectuera les paiements en recourant à la méthode de décaissement par Paiement direct, comme définie dans les Directives de la Banque Mondiale applicables aux Décaissements dans le cadre de Financements de Projets d’Investissement, à l’exception des paiements pour lesquels le marché stipule que le paiement sera effectué par crédit documentaire.

2.  L’Unité de Coordination et de Management des Projets (UCM) du Ministère des Ressources Hydrauliques et de l’Electricité invite, par la présente, les Proposants de pays éligibles à remettre des Propositions sous pli fermé, pour la réalisation d’un Système Intégré d’Information de Gestion comprenant un progiciel de gestion intégré, un système de gestion commerciale, un système de gestion des incidents et un système d’information géographique pour la Société Nationale d’Electricité (SNEL SA) qui sera principalement logé à la Direction Générale de la Société Nationale d’Electricité (SNEL SA) à Kinshasa, en RDC dans un délai de dix-huit (18) mois.

4.  Les Offres seront évaluées conformément au processus d'évaluation défini dans le dossier d'appel d'offres. Les pondérations suivantes s'appliqueront aux Critères notés (y compris les facteurs techniques et autres que le prix) : 60 % et pour le coût de l'Offre : 40 %.

La passation de marchés électronique ne sera pas autorisée.

Les enveloppes extérieures de la Proposition portant la mention « PROPOSITION ORIGINALE » et les enveloppes intérieures portant la mention « PARTIE TECHNIQUE » seront ouvertes au public en présence des représentants désignés du Proposant et de toute personne qui choisira d’y assister, à l’adresse ci-dessous le même lundi 28 septembre 2026 à 15h30’ (heure locale, TU+1).

  1. The Georgia financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Georgia I2Q - Innovation, Inclusion and Quality Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for Procurement of Educational Resources and Technical Equipment for Robotics Innovation Spaces.
  2. The Ministry of Education, Science and Youth of Georgia (MESY) now invites Bids from eligible Bidders for Procurement of Educational Resources and Technical Equipment for Robotics Innovation Spaces. Delivery time of goods is 70 calendar days from the date of Contract Signature. Delivery destination is LLC "Educational Resources", Address: 4 Ivan Yumashevi Street, Tbilisi, Georgia.
  3. Bidding will be conducted through national competitive procurement using a Request for Bids (RFB) as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, July 2016 revised September 2025” (“Procurement Regulations”) and is open to all eligible Bidders as defined in the Procurement Regulations.
  4. Bidders shall submit their bids ONLY electronically through Georgian E-Government Procurement System: https://tenders.procurement.gov.ge/login.php?lang=en
  5. Bid opening will take place electronically using Georgian E-Government Procurement System with certain modifications. Major modifications to the Georgian E-Procurement System are:
  • Functionality of the three rounds of e-Reverse auction is removed. Rounds will not be applicable.
  • The estimated cost of the contract is disclosed in the e-Procurement system and bidders can submit a bid price, which could be below or above the estimated cost, however pricing the bid is the responsibility of the bidder which shall be based on the current market prices and any other factors which may influence the pricing of the proposed works.

6. The Bidders shall obtain the Tender Documentation on the following link:

https://tenders.procurement.gov.ge/public/?go=699822&lang=ge

7. Instruction for registration on the E-Procurement System can be found on the following link:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hQak4jPorj4&feature=youtu.be

8. Instruction for bidding on the E-Procurement System can be found on the following link:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9O3W8_WiDgg&feature=youtu.be

9. Requests for clarification should be submitted through the Georgian E-Government Procurement System.

If there is discrepancy between the Georgian E-Government Procurement System read out price and bid price mentioned in the uploaded bid document, then the bid price mentioned in the uploaded bid will prevail. The bid price mentioned in the letter of bid and price schedules in the uploaded bid will be evaluated as per the provisions mentioned in the bidding document.

10. The minimum qualification criteria for Bidders to participate in the tender are:

(a) Financial Capability: The Bidder shall submit audited financial statements for the last three (3) years (2023, 2024, and 2025) or, if such statements are not required by the laws of the Bidder’s country, other financial statements acceptable to the Purchaser, demonstrating the Bidder’s current sound financial position. As a minimum, the Bidder’s net worth for the last year calculated as the difference between total assets and total liabilities should be positive. For a Joint Venture, this requirement shall be met by each member of the Joint Venture.

(b) Specific Experience: The Bidder shall demonstrate that it has successfully completed at least three (3) contracts during the last five (5) years (2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025), each with a contract value of at least USD 50,000 or equivalent, which have been successfully and substantially completed and are similar in nature and complexity to the Goods under this Contract (Supply of STEAM Resourses/ Computers/Other Types of Equipment/Hardware). For a Joint Venture, this requirement may be met by the combined experience of all members of the Joint Venture. For evaluation purposes, the currency exchange rate applicable on the date of contract signature, as published by the National Bank of Georgia, shall be used to convert the contract value into the currency specified for evaluation.

(c) Manufacturing experience and Technical Capacity: For the items under the Contract that the bidder is a manufacturer, the Bidder shall furnish documentary evidence to demonstrate that:

(i)   it has manufactured goods of similar nature and complexity for at least three (3) years 2023, 2024, and 2025, and

(ii)  its annual production capacity of goods of similar nature and complexity, for each of the years 2023, 2024, and 2025, is at least two (2) times the quantities specified under the Contract.

(d) A bidder who does not manufacture an item shall submit documentation on, its status as a supplier, to the satisfaction of the Purchaser (e.g. authorized dealer/ distributor of the items).

At the time of Contract Award, the Bidder (including each subcontractor proposed by the Bidder) shall not be subject to disqualification by the Bank for non-compliance with SEA/ SH obligations.

11. All Bids must be accompanied by a Bid-Securing Declaration. The Bid Security Declaration shall be valid for 28 days beyond the validity of the Bid (i.e., 90 days+28 days = 118 days). For bids submitted by a JV bidder shall carefully read ITB 19.8 as failure to comply with this ITB may be grounds for bid rejection.

procnotices.notice_text:
APPEL A CANDIDATURES

Assistant Technique en Infrastructure FDL

AMI N° : 563407/26/AMI/UNGP/MIONJO

1. Le Gouvernement de la République de Madagascar a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour couvrir le coût du Projet soutien aux moyens de subsistance résilients dans le Sud de Madagascar « MIONJO » et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce fonds à des services de consultant.

2. Les services de consultant (« les Services ») viseront à appuyer le Fonds de Développement Local dans la réalisation de toutes les activités liées à la mise en œuvre des projets de construction et/ou de réhabilitation d'infrastructures.

3. Les Termes de Référence (TDR) pour la mission sont disponibles sur le site internet suivant : https://mionjo.mg ou sur demande à adresser à procurement@mionjo.mg.

4. L'Unité Nationale de Gestion du Projet (UNGP) MIONJO invite dès à présent les consultants admissibles (« Consultants ») à faire part de leur intérêt à fournir les Services. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l’expérience pertinente pour exécuter les Services. Les critères de sélection sont les suivants :

Qualifications et expériences :

  • Titulaire d'un diplôme d'ingénieur en Bâtiment et Travaux publics ou Ingénieur Civil de Construction (BACC+5) ;
  • Expérience professionnelle d'au moins cinq (05) ans dans le domaine de la gestion de projets d ' infrastructures ;
  • Expérience d'au moins trois (03) ans dans la Conception et Dessin Assistés par Ordinateur (AutoCAD, ArchiCAD, Covadis ;
  • Connaissance en Maîtrise d 'Ouvrage Publique, Passation et Gestion de Marchés publics, suivi-évaluation des projets ;
  • Maîtrise de la suite logiciels office de Microsoft Apte au fréquent déplacement en milieu rural ;

Atouts :

  • Connaissance en Décentralisation et Développement Local Connaissance en Gestion environnementale des projets d'infrastructures ;

Les candidats qualifiés seront convoqués à un entretien et/ou à un test écrit.

5. L’attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes, 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs de FPI » de la Banque mondiale, Septième Edition Septembre 2025 (« Règlement de Passation des Marchés »), qui énonce la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d’intérêts.  En outre, veuillez-vous reporter aux informations spécifiques suivantes sur les conflits d’intérêts liés à cette mission : « Le Consultant qui a une relation professionnelle ou familiale étroite avec tout cadre de l’Emprunteur, de l’organisme d’exécution du projet, d’un bénéficiaire d’une fraction du financement de la Banque ou de toute autre partie représentant l’Emprunteur ou agissant en son nom qui participe directement ou indirectement à tout segment : (i) de la préparation des Termes de référence de la mission ; (ii) du processus de sélection pour le contrat ; ou (iii) de la supervision du contrat, ne peut être attributaire d’un contrat, sauf si le conflit résultant de ladite relation a été réglé d’une manière que la Banque juge satisfaisante tout au long du processus de sélection et de l’exécution du contrat »..

6. Un Consultant sera sélectionné conformément aux dispositions décrites dans le Règlement de Passation des Marchés.

7. Des informations supplémentaires peuvent être obtenues à l’adresse ci-dessous pendant les heures de bureau de 09h00 à 17h00, heures locales.

8. Les manifestations d’intérêt contenant (i) une lettre de motivation avec prétention salariale rédigée en français, (ii) un CV détaillé mise à jour (modèle en annexe aux TDRs) et (iii) les copies des diplômes et le Certificats prouvant les expériences professionnelles, seront adressées au Coordonnateur du Projet MIONJO et envoyées à l’adresse ci-dessous (en personne, par la poste, ou par courriel) au plus tard le 21 Août 2026.

 

Adresse : Lot II A 105 G Nanisana Iadiambola, Antananarivo 101

Courriel : procuremen@mionjo.mg  et rpm@mionjo.mg

Et portant la mention « AMI N° 563407/26/AMI/UNGP/MIONJO – Assistant Technique en Infrastructure FDL»

Antananarivo le, 22 juillet 2026

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

UGANDA

UGANDA DIGITAL ACCELERATION PROJECT – GOVERNMENT NETWORK (UDAP-GOVNET)

PROJECT ID-P171305

LOAN NUMBER: IDA-68980

REFERENCE NUMBER: NITA-UDAP/CONS/26-27/0004

ASSIGNMENT TITLE:  CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF A NATIONAL DIGITAL SKILLS AND COMPETENCE FRAMEWORK (NDSCF)

 

The Government of Uganda, represented by the National Information Technology Authority - Uganda (NITA-U), has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Uganda Digital Acceleration Project - Government Network (UDAP-GOVNET) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consultancy services for the development of a National Digital Skills and Competence Framework (NDSCF).

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) include consultancy services for the development of a National Digital Skills and Competence Framework (NDSCF).

 

The primary objective of this assignment is to develop a comprehensive, standardized, and future-oriented National Digital Skills and Competence Framework (NDSCF) for Uganda, serving as the foundation for all digital-skilling interventions under UDAP and beyond, aligned to national development priorities, responsive to labour-market demand, and inclusive of all population groups including those most at risk of exclusion from the digital economy.

 

The Implementation period of the assignment is six (6) Months from the date of signing the contract.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment are attached to this Expression of Interest.

 

The National Information Technology Authority - Uganda now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

 

The Shortlisting Criteria for the firm’s capacity and experience are:

  1. A minimum of ten (10) years of core business as a consultant in undertaking ICT, education technology, research, or management consultancy.
  2. Submit the firm’s organogram to demonstrate the firm’s technical and managerial capability;
  3. The firm shall demonstrate completion of at least Five (5) assignments involving the design or implementation of a national digital-skills, ICT-competency, or digital-literacy framework, with documented adoption, validation, or endorsement by a government ministry, regulator, or statutory agency within the past seven (07) years.
  4. Presence of appropriate skills among staff; Team Leader / Framework Architect, Senior Digital Competency and Curriculum Specialist, AI and Emerging Technology Specialist, Assessment, Certification and Qualifications Specialist, Cybersecurity Specialist, Gender, Disability and Social Inclusion Specialist, Research and Data Science Specialist, EdTech, Instructional Design Specialist, Uganda Policy and Stakeholder Engagement Specialist, Monitoring and Evaluation Specialist. (please do not submit CVs and biodata of experts at this stage).

 

The attention of interested consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.15 and 3.16, of the World Bank’s ‘Procurement in Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, Seventh Edition September 2025 (Procurement in investment Project Financing; Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications.

 

A consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations “Procurement in Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, Seventh Edition September 2025”.

 

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours at the address below 08:00 to 17:00 hours from Monday to Friday at the address given below.

 

Expressions of Interest (One original plus two copies) must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person or by e-mail) on or before Wednesday, 26th August 2026

 at 11:00am Consultants not located in the Country may submit their REOIs through the provided email address.

 

The packages must be clearly marked as; “Expression of Interest for consultancy services for the development of a National Digital Skills and Competence Framework (NDSCF)”

 

The Procurement Officer,

National Information Technology Authority-Uganda Palm Courts, Plot 7A Rotary Avenue,1st Floor Kampala-Uganda,

Email: steven.batte@nita.go.ug

 

Any form of canvassing or lobbying for the tender shall lead to automatic disqualification.

EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR.

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

Inclusive Service Delivery and Digital Transformation in Indonesia

Loan No. IBRD-95200-ID

Project ID No. P175218

Assignment Title

:

Strengthening Customer Relationship Management and the Population Administration Service Improvement Survey Consulting Firm

Reference No

:

ID-DITJEN DUKCAPIL-552206-CS-CQS

The Government of Indonesia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of Inclusive Service Delivery and Digital Transformation in Indonesia (Loan No. IBRD-95200), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

To respond to the increasing needs and challenges in population administration and to utilize the strategic role of accurate population data, the Government of Indonesia has initiated comprehensive efforts to modernize and strengthen its system. This commitment is reflected in the launch of the project "ID for Inclusive Service Delivery and Digital Transformation in Indonesia," which aims to improve the population and civil registration framework and introduce secure digital identity solutions. Through this initiative, Indonesia seeks to ensure that all citizens and residents can access inclusive, efficient, and digitally integrated public and private services, thereby supporting national development goals and digital transformation.

In general, the scope of work for this consultant service includes:

I. Implementation of an Independent Public Satisfaction Survey (IKM). The Consulting Firm shall design and implement the Public Satisfaction Index (IKM) survey on population administration services, to be conducted twice:

  1. in 2026 as a baseline measurement, and
  2. in 2027 as a comparative survey to assess improvements in public satisfaction over time.

II. Development of Recommendations for Strengthening an Integrated CRM System.

The Consulting Firm shall develop comprehensive recommendations to strengthen DG Dukcapil’s integrated Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system, ensuring that both citizens and institutional users have access to feedback mechanisms that are secure, traceable, and responsive, thereby supporting citizen-centric service delivery and enhancing service satisfaction.

The duration of project task implementation is estimated to be (14) fourteen months and the location of task implementation is located in Jakarta.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below:

https://bit.ly/452gZsE

The Ministry of Home Affairs, Directorate General of Population and Civil Registration now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the services. Interested Consultants should provide information to demonstrate that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services such as brochures/company profile (indicating the core of business and technical resources) and description of similar assignments (including location/country, name of the Client, type of services provided, contract amount, period of contract, including the starting and the completion date) and contract value.

The shortlisting criteria are:

A. Core Business and year in Business:

At least 10 (ten) years’ experience in management consulting. A legally established national, international, or local consulting firm with a minimum of ten (10) years of experience in management consulting. Joint ventures are permitted.

B. Similar experiences required:

Consultant must have successfully carried out all required experiences as follows:

  1. Has experience in developing survey instruments for national-scale surveys in Indonesia in at least two (2) projects within the last five (5) years, including conducting field surveys, analyzing survey data, and presenting survey results.
  2. Experience in survey activities related to government public services/government regulations will be considered an added value, by attaching a list of the relevant experience.
  3. Has experience in at least two (2) projects within the last five (5) years in developing recommendations for CRM governance and/or CRM systems, by attaching a list of the relevant experience.
  4. Possesses valid ISO 9001 Quality Management System certification and ISO/IEC 27001 Information Security Management System certification.

C. Technical and Managerial capability of the firm:

Availability within the firm of permanent (i.e. in the firm’s regular payroll), experts/ professional staff relevant to the assignment. Provide only the structure of the organization, general qualifications, and number of related key staff. Do not provide CV’s of the staff. The consultant may add list of its experts but should note that all experts qualifications will not be evaluated at this stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Fifth Edition September 2020 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

A Firm will be selected in accordance with the CQS (Consultant’s Qualifications-based Selection) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Consultants may associate with other Firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a subconcultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. In case of Joint Venture, the member firm appointed to represent the joint venture must be clearly identified.

Further information can be obtained at the address or email below during office hours 07:30 to 16:00 hours (Western Indonesia Time).

Expressions of Interest (EOI) must be submitted electronically through SPSE ICB system of LKPP no later than September 2nd, 2026 at 16:00 (Jakarta Time).

For the project experience list, please follow the template provided in the following link: https://bit.ly/452gZsE

procnotices.bid_description: Management Support Consultant (MSC)  for Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Hydropower & Renewable Energy Development (KHRE) Program - Pakhtunkhwa Energy Development Organization (PEDO)
procnotices.contact_address: Plot No. 38, Sect B-2, Phase-5 Hayatabad, Peshawar
procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

KHYBER PAKHTUNKHWA HYDROPOWER & RENEWABLE ENERGY DEVELOPMENT (KHRE) PROGRAM

ASSIGNMENT TITLE: MANAGEMENT SUPPORT CONSULTANT (MSC)

1. Background

The Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (GoKP), through the Pakhtunkhwa Energy Development Organization (PEDO), is implementing the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Hydropower & Renewable Energy Development (KHRE) Program with financial assistance of the World Bank.

The objective of the Program is to support the development of hydropower and renewable energy resources in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, strengthen institutional capacity, and improve the operational, commercial, and governance frameworks of PEDO.

In this regard, PEDO intends to engage a qualified Consulting Firm as a Management Support Consultant (MSC) to provide institutional strengthening, strategic advisory, implementation support, and capacity development services.

2. Scope of Services

The Consultant shall provide services including, but not limited to, the following areas:

  • Institutional review and organizational restructuring
  • Human Resource Management (HRM) framework development
  • Financial management, budgeting, and investment planning
  • Tariff, commercial, and regulatory advisory
  • Procurement and contract management strengthening
  • ERP and Project Monitoring Information System (PMIS) advisory
  • Legal and regulatory framework support
  • Capacity building, change management, and institutional reforms

The assignment is expected to be carried out over a period of at least one and half (1.5 years) at PEDO Headquarters, Peshawar, including travel to project sites and field offices, where required.

3. Request for Expressions of Interest

Pakhtunkhwa Energy Development Organization now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services.

Interested firms should provide information demonstrating that they possess the required qualifications, relevant experience, and technical capability to perform the assignment.

The shortlisting criteria are:

  • Minimum ten (10) years of relevant experience in public-sector institutional reforms, organizational strengthening, and power  sector advisory services
  • Successful completion of at least three (03) similar assignments during the last ten (10) years, preferably in the power and renewable energy sectors
  • Demonstrated experience in providing advisory, institutional strengthening, and implementation support services in areas including institutional reforms, financial management, procurement and contract management, ERP systems, legal/regulatory frameworks, and tariff/commercial matters
  • Prior experience in assignments funded by the World Bank or other international development partners
  • Demonstrated availability of qualified multidisciplinary experts relevant to the assignment
  • Experience in developing countries and strong knowledge of the Pakistan’s power sector regulatory environment shall be considered an advantage

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

4. Association with Other Firms

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint-venture and/or a sub-consultancy.

In the case of a joint venture, all partners shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

5. Selection Method

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (latest edition).

Attention of interested Consultants is drawn to the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers regarding conflict-of-interest provisions applicable to this assignment.

6. Submission Requirements

Interested firms shall submit the following information:

  • Company profile and organizational details
  • Relevant experience and similar assignments completed
  • Details of assignments of similar nature and complexity
  • Experience with donor-funded projects
  • Availability of relevant technical expertise and resources
  • Contact details of authorized representative

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TORs) may be obtained from the address given below during office hours (0900 to 1700 hours) Monday through Friday or down-loaded from PEDO website:  https://pedokp.gov.pk

7. Submission of Expressions of Interest

Expressions of Interest must be delivered in written form no later than 02 October 2026 at 1100 hours (Pakistan Standard Time) through courier, mail, email, or by hand to the address below.

The Assignment Title “Management Support Consultant (MSC)” shall be clearly mentioned on the submission.

8. Address for Submission

 

 

Chief Engineer / Head PMO, KHRE

Ground Floor, NESPAK Building (PEDO-WB PMO Project Office),

Plot # 24, Sector: B/2, Phase-5, Hayatabad, Peshawar, Pakistam

Tel: +92 91 9219616- 7

 pd.mdhpp@pedo.pk

Late submissions shall not be entertained.

procnotices.project_name: West Bank and Gaza Social Recovery and Job Creation Project
procnotices.bid_description: MoLG: Development Decentralized Wastewater Treatment Consultant
procnotices.contact_address: Ramalla
procnotices.contact_organization: Ministry of Planning and International Cooperation
procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

Individual Consultant Services

Decentralized Wastewater Treatment Consultant

Social Recovery and Job Creation Project (SRJC)

The Ministry of Finance and Planning (MoFP), through the Social Recovery and Job Creation Project (SRJC), invites qualified individual consultants to express their interest in providing consulting services for conducting Decentralized Wastewater Treatment for the benefit of the Ministry of Local Government.

Background

The Social Recovery and Job Creation Project (SRJC) is financed by the World Bank and implemented under the overall oversight of the Ministry of Finance and Planning (MoFP). The project aims to:

  1. Increase employment opportunities for selected groups in targeted areas; and
  2. Improve the operational capacity of selected government institutions.

Under Component 3, Capacity Building of Selected Government Institutions, the Ministry of Local Government (MoLG) is implementing a capacity-building programme aimed at strengthening its institutional and technical capacities and enhancing the delivery of sustainable and resilient local public services.

As part of this programme, the Ministry seeks to strengthen its technical guidance for sustainable wastewater management. Many Palestinian Local Government Units (LGUs) continue to face challenges in providing wastewater services due to limited financial and technical capacities, the high costs of centralized systems, and environmental, planning, and geographical constraints, particularly in rural and underserved areas.

To address these challenges, the Ministry intends to engage an Individual Consultant to develop a Technical Guidance Manual for Decentralized Wastewater Treatment Solutions. The assignment will support the Ministry and LGUs in planning, selecting, and implementing sustainable wastewater treatment solutions that are technically feasible, environmentally sound, and aligned with national priorities.

Assignment Objective

The objective of this assignment is to support Ministry of Local Government (MoLG) in developing a Technical Guidance Manual for Decentralized Wastewater Treatment Solutions and to strengthen the capacity of MoLG and LGUs in planning, selecting, and implementing sustainable wastewater management solutions.

The assignment includes assessing existing needs, identifying priority locations, evaluating appropriate technology options, and developing technical guidance to support informed decision-making and the selection of solutions that are technically feasible, environmentally and socially sound, responsive to local conditions, and aligned with national priorities.

Scope of the Assignment

Under the overall supervision of the Ministry of Local Government, the Consultant shall provide technical expertise to support the development of a Technical Guidance Manual for Decentralized Wastewater Treatment Solutions for Palestinian Local Government Units.

The proposed solutions and technical guidance shall be aligned with the relevant strategies and requirements of MoLG and the Palestinian Water Authority (PWA), as well as the applicable national reform and development plans.

The Consultant shall also prepare operational guidance as part of the assignment.

3.1 Main Duties and Responsibilities

The Consultant shall be responsible for, but not limited to, the following:

  1. Review relevant legislation, policies, strategies, technical guidelines, and existing studies related to wastewater management and decentralized wastewater treatment systems.
  2. Develop practical and scalable criteria for selecting appropriate decentralized wastewater treatment solutions, in full coordination with MoLG and with due consideration to operation and maintenance requirements.
  3. Assess the current status of wastewater management and identify the main technical, institutional, environmental, financial, and operational challenges faced by Palestinian Local Government Units.
  4. Assess existing wastewater management needs and develop objective criteria for identifying priority locations suitable for decentralized wastewater treatment solutions.
  5. Identify and evaluate appropriate small-scale decentralized wastewater treatment technologies and models applicable to different local contexts, taking into consideration:
    • Technical feasibility.
    • Environmental and social mitigation measures.
    • Sustainability.
    • Operation and maintenance requirements.
    • Cost-effectiveness.
  6. Develop a Technical Guidance Manual for Decentralized Wastewater Treatment Solutions to support LGUs in selecting and planning appropriate wastewater management solutions.
  7. Prepare preliminary conceptual designs for selected priority locations, as appropriate.
  8. Conduct meetings and consultations with MoLG and relevant stakeholders, including PWA and PEA, throughout the assignment.
  9. Prepare and submit all required reports and deliverables, including the Inception Report, Assessment Report, Draft Technical Guidance Manual, Final Report, and Presentation, while incorporating comments received from MoLG.
  10. Ensure effective coordination with all relevant stakeholders, including MoLG, PWA, and PEA.
  11. Perform any other related tasks requested by MoLG within the agreed scope of the assignment.

Key Deliverables

The Consultant shall submit the following deliverables:

No.

Deliverable

Description

1

Inception Report

A comprehensive report outlining the assignment methodology, detailed work plan, implementation schedule, and stakeholder engagement approach.

2

Assessment Report

A detailed report assessing the current status of wastewater management in Palestinian Local Government Units and identifying the main challenges, existing gaps, and priority locations suitable for decentralized wastewater treatment solutions.

3

Draft Technical Guidance Manual

A draft Technical Guidance Manual presenting appropriate decentralized wastewater treatment technologies, technical selection criteria, preliminary conceptual designs for selected priority locations, implementation guidance, and operation and maintenance considerations to support MoLG and LGUs in planning and implementing sustainable wastewater treatment solutions.

4

Final Report and Presentation

A final report incorporating the comments of the Ministry of Local Government. The report shall include the finalized Technical Guidance Manual, selection criteria, operational guidance contributing to the capacity building of MoLG engineering staff and LGU staff, recommendations for improving service delivery, preliminary conceptual and economic designs, implementation guidance, documentation of consultations with key stakeholders, and a presentation summarizing the key findings of the assignment.

All deliverables shall be submitted to and formally approved by the Ministry of Local Government.

Reporting and Coordination

The Consultant shall work under the overall supervision of the Ministry of Local Government and shall closely coordinate with the relevant departments and stakeholders throughout the assignment.

The Consultant shall report directly to the designated focal point within MoLG and shall submit all reports, deliverables, and other required outputs for review and approval in accordance with the agreed work plan and timeline.

The Consultant shall maintain regular communication with the Ministry, participate in coordination meetings as requested, present the key findings and recommendations, and address comments received from the Ministry to ensure that all deliverables meet the required quality standards and the objectives of the assignment.

Duration of Assignment

The duration of the assignment shall be six (6) months from the date of signature.

Estimated Level of Effort

The Consultant shall provide the level of effort required to satisfactorily complete all tasks and deliver all outputs specified in these Terms of Reference within the contract period.

The estimated level of effort is fifty (50) working days.

Duty Station

The Consultant will be based at the Ministry of Local Government Headquarters in Ramallah, Palestine.

The Consultant shall undertake five (5) field visits to selected Local Government Units and project sites, as required and in coordination with the Ministry, to effectively carry out the assignment.

Required Qualifications and Experience

The Consultant shall have the following qualifications and experience:

  • At least a Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Water Engineering, Sanitary Engineering, or another closely related discipline. Higher academic qualifications in a relevant field will be considered an asset.
  • Relevant professional experience in wastewater management, wastewater treatment, sanitation, and related infrastructure projects, demonstrating suitability for the assignment.
  • Demonstrated technical experience in decentralized wastewater treatment systems, technical assessments, development of technical models, conceptual designs, or other related wastewater management assignments.
  • Experience working with public-sector institutions and/or donor-funded projects, preferably projects financed by international development partners.
  • Strong reporting, communication, coordination, and networking skills.

Selection Method and Evaluation Criteria

The Consultant will be selected in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers and based on the qualifications and experience of the applicant.

The evaluation will be conducted out of a total score of 100 points as follows:

Points

Evaluation Criterion

10

At least a Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Water Engineering, Sanitary Engineering, or another closely related discipline. Higher academic qualifications in a relevant field will be considered an asset.

40

Relevant professional experience in wastewater management, wastewater treatment, sanitation, and related infrastructure projects, demonstrating suitability and adequacy for the assignment.

25

Demonstrated technical experience in decentralized wastewater treatment systems, technical assessments, development of technical models, conceptual designs, or other related wastewater management assignments.

10

Experience working with public-sector institutions and/or donor-funded projects, preferably projects financed by international development partners.

15

Reporting, communication, coordination, and networking skills.

100

Total

 

Only candidates obtaining a minimum technical score of 70 points may be invited for an interview, if deemed necessary by the evaluation committee.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (REOI)

 

Reference No: PwD-REoI-PMTC-002

Name of Project

Loan No/Credit No/ Grand Number

Assignment Title

 

 

Selection of a Consultancy firm for “Design, Management & Supervision Consultant for Construction of New Public Buildings including Emergency Shelters, Retrofitting & Augmentation of existing Public Buildings and allied works” for the Public Works Department under the READY-HP Project

Borrower

Government of Himachal Pradesh

Implementing Agency

India

The Government of Himachal Pradesh has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Resilient Action for Development and Disaster Recovery in Himachal Pradesh (READY-HP) project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for the following consulting services.

The objective of the consultancy (“the Services”) is to engage Technical Consultants to provide specialized engineering, advisory and supervision support to the PIU housed in HPPWD Shimla for the effective delivery of the READY-HP Project. The Technical Consultant will be responsible for(i) overall project management of the buildings and emergency shelters investments, (ii) preparing Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) for the major maintenance, strengthening, rehabilitation, retrofitting, and reconstruction of damaged buildings, (iii) design and supervision of new buildings and emergency shelters and (iv) providing end-to-end technical assistance throughout the project lifecycle. The duration of the services will be 48 months with (i) DPR preparation, environmental and social assessments (ESAs) and commensurate mitigation plans, and associated studies (to be delivered in the first 12 months) and other scope as per TORs(ii) construction supervision support (months 13– 48, however, this timeline is indicative and supervision support could start earlier in case of early award of civil works contracts),and (iii) project management services, including carry out training and capacity building as per agreed annual roaster (throughout the 48 months of contract duration).

The Himachal Pradesh Public Works Department (HPPWD) invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services described in EOI. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they fulfill the below-mentioned qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services: -

 

Shortlisting criteria are as under: -

Sl. No.

 Eligibility Criteria

 Evaluation Parameters

Supporting Documents to be submitted / Remarks

1

Experience of the Firm

(i)Minimum 10 years’ experience in consultancy services in India in World Bank assisted projects or other State/Central/Multilateral Financial Institution funded projects.

  • Brief organization profile, including year of establishment.
  • List of relevant assignments over the last 5 years, including project title, duration, scope, contract value (firm’s share), client reference, and supporting documentation.

 

  • Valid PAN, GST, and organization registration certificates.

(ii)Experience in preparation of DPRs for Building / Emergency Shelter projects, including providing Architectural Design, Structural Design, Building Services, Technical Advisory, Supervision services with government agencies at the National or State level, public sector. Minimum 3projects in the last 5 years. Among these, at least:

(a) Have completed one DPR of projects funded by the World Bank or any multilateral/bilateral agencies or national and state level agencies or the public sector for Building/Shelter works each of consultancy value >Rs 100 lakhs.

(b)Have completed one DPR of projects in rehabilitation, retrofitting and reconstruction of consultancy in buildings/emergency shelters value >Rs. 50lakhs.

 

(c) Have completed one DPRs of projects executed in hilly terrain for buildings, each of consultancy value >Rs. 25 lakhs.

2

Staff Experience and Qualifications

Demonstrate capacity to deploy a qualified multidisciplinary team comprising experts in structural design (new building construction and retrofitting), geotechnical engineering, construction management, environment and social management and project management for this assignment as detailed in ToRs.

The Proposed Team of experts shall preferably have experience with Multilateral Development Bank /World Bank-funded projects as stated in the ToRs.

  • Confirmation of availability of Team Leader + Key Experts with qualifications and relevant experience.

(CVs not required at this stage)

Confirmation regarding availability of resources with a summary of qualifications and project experience.

The firm shall confirm availability of key personnel/Experts.

 

(No individual CVs are required at this stage)

3

Financial Capacity

The firm shall have a Minimum annual turnover of Rs 15Cr in any one of the last three financial years in technical consultancy services.

Audited Financial Reports and CA Certificate for the last three financial years.

4

Legal & Statutory Compliance

Firm must be legally registered and compliant with all statutory requirements

• Firm registration certificate

 • PAN

 • GST registration

5

Non-suspension/Debarment

The firm should not be debarred/ suspended for non-performance by Govt. of HP/Govt. of India. Or sanctioned or debarred by the World Bank or multilateral/bilateral agency/

A declaration by the firm confirming as stated.

The attention of interested Firms is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of section III of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” (February 2025), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with one other firm in the form of a Joint Venture (JV) or a sub-consultancy. However, for evaluation and short listing of REoI, the eligibility criteria of the lead member/ primary consultant shall only be considered. Further details in this regard shall be made available in the RFP document.

All firms must meet the eligibility requirements under the World Bank Procurement Regulations, including those related to debarment, sanctions, and conflict of interest.

A Consultant will finally be selected in accordance with the Consultant Qualification-based Selection(CQS) method based on the criteria set out in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” (February 2025).

Further information may be obtained from the address below during office hours (10:00 hours to 17:00 hours IST), except on State Government holidays.

Expression of Interest (EoI) with the accompanying information must be delivered in the written form (with five hard copies) in a sealed envelope addressed to the Superintending Engineer (QC&D/READY-HP), Project Implementation Unit (PIU) of HPPWD in the Government of

Himachal Pradesh by 16.00 hours (IST) of 17th August, 2026 at the address below. The REoI shall be opened on 17th August, 2026 16:30 Hrs.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(INDIVIDUAL CONSULTING SERVICES)

 

Republic of the Marshall Islands

Early Children Development II

 

Loan No./Credit No./ Grant No.: IDA-E0320

Assignment Title: International Consultant: National ECD Action Plan & Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEAL) framework

Reference No.: MH-ECD PMO-564509-CS-INDV                                         

 

The Government is seeking to hire an International Consultant: National ECD Action Plan & Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEAL) framework to assist the Early Childhood Development project (ECD) and GRMI efforts in translating policy into a strategic time-bound measureable Action Plan and update the Monitoring and Evaluation Plan. The ECD Policy consultant will be responsible to review in-depth the existing draft Action Plan for each Strategic Priority under the national ECD policy and other relevant documents. The consultant will also Conduct consultation with all relevant government ministries and agencies responsible for implementing the activities and achieving results under each strategic priority, including development partners supporting the government ministries/agencies with technical assistance and/or financing for the ECD related outcome areas. Additionally, the consultant will propose modification and enhancement to the specific objectives, actions to be taken and targets to be achieved within each priority area, including who is responsible, timeline, and resources needed. Incorporate into the Action Plan salient developments in the country context, in terms of government policies and programs relevant to the ECD agenda. Consider to include in the Action Plan, where relevant, key national priorities and global agenda which might not have been adequately reflected in current draft, such as Climate Change, Nuclear Legacy, Social-emotional (Mental) well-being, and economic empowerment.

 

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) can be found at: hr.rmi.ecd@gmail.com

The Office of the Chief Secretary now invites eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (attach curriculum vitae with description of experience in similar assignments, similar conditions, etc.). Firms’ staff may express interest through the employing firm for the assignment and, under such situation, only the experience and qualifications of individuals shall be considered in the selection process. The criteria for selecting the Consultant are:

Mandatory Qualification and Experience

  1. At a minimum, a master’s degree in relevant academic fields such as public policy, development, governance, social sciences with focus in early childhood development subjects
  2. At least 7 years of relevant international experience in working with governments and/or international/development agencies on technical and policy aspects related to the early childhood development (health and nutrition, early childhood education, social assistance/social protection)
  3. Technical expertise and strong understanding of MEL principles, methodologies and best practices
  4. Demonstrated experience in developing national MEL frameworks and engaging diverse stakeholders in the government (national and subnational level), preferably in a similar context. 
  5. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
  6. Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English language

 

Desired Qualification and Experience

  1. Experience working in developing countries with appreciation of RMI, Micronesia and/ or Pacific Region is highly desirable.
  2. Experience working on/with World Bank or other international donor-funded projects.
  3. Experience in training, capacity building and coaching/mentoring of government staff, CSOs and local stakeholders
  4. Ability to work independently and as part of the multi-sectoral and multi-cultural team, both remotely and in person

 

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by fax, or by e-mail) by September 1st 2026

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

 

CONSULTING SERVICES ON STRENGTHENING THE LEVEL OF COMPETENCE AND KNOW HOW TRANSFER ON OPERATION OF THE METROLOGY EQUIPMENT (1ST BATCH)

 

 

REPUBLIC OF MOLDOVA

MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM-SIZED ENTERPRISES COMPETITIVENESS PROJECT

Sector: General industry and trade sector

IDA Credit No. 71740

IBRD Loan No. 94230

Project ID No. P177895

Reference No. MD-CEP-547270-CS-CQS

 

The Republic of Moldova has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Micro, Small and Medium-Sized Enterprise Competitiveness Project (MSME) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) include enhancement the technical competence and knowledge in the field of mass metrology of Moldovan NMI specialists through comprehensive training and structured know-how transfer, focusing on both theoretical knowledge and practical skills in the following domains: (i) Mass measurements; (ii) Length measurements; (iii) Pressure measurements and (iv) Force measurements. To achieve the assignment’s objectives, the Consultant shall develop the training materials and deliver trainings for NMI specialists at the NMI premises and ensure practical on-site trainings for specialists of NMI at Consultant’ premises according to the topics, duration and timeline suggested in ToR.

 

The assignment will be performed in the period May - July, 2026.  

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment is attached to this request for expressions of interest.

 

The Project Implementation Unit of the MSME Competitiveness Project now invites eligible local consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (required qualifications and experience of the firm, but not individual experts’ bio data).

 

This assignment will require an EURAMET metrology institute or consortium of such metrology institutes with appropriate technical and metrological qualification, comparable standards and internationally recognized knowledge, which:

  • Has relevant competence in the field of length, mass pressure and force measurements including relevant Calibration and Measurement Capabilities in the Bureau International des Poids et Measures (BIPM) key comparison database.
  • Has demonstrated previous experience in providing similar internship and/or trainings in relevant subject fields.
  • Has experience in the implementation of the donors’ and/or IFI’s sponsored projects.
  • Has experience in preparation of analytical reports, training programs and training curricula.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” November 2020 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.  A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the „Consultant’s Qualification-based Selection” method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications; but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

 

The Expression of Interest shall clearly state the name of the Consultant (individual Firm, Joint Venture or sub-consultancy). The Consultant shall provide relevant references (assignment name, Client, time frame, the role of the firm (main Consultant/Partner in JV/sub-consultant, contract amount, tasks performed etc.) to confirm its experience and qualifications.

 

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours.

 

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by e-mail) by May 11, 2026, COB.

 

Project Implementation Unit of the MSME Competitiveness Project

180, Stefan cel Mare Ave., office 815, MD-2004, Chisinau, Republic of Moldova

Tel:  + 373 22 296-723

e-mail: piu@mded.gov.md

web:     www.uipac.md

 

E-mail for submission of the clarifications: piu@mded.gov.md

 

E-mail for submission of the EoIs: procurementmgf@gmail.com 

 

Only the notification of EoI submission must be sent to piu@mded.gov.md
 Terms of Reference

Consulting Services on strengthening the level of competence and know how transfer on operation of the metrology equipment (1st batch)  

 

A.           INTRODUCTION

The Government of the Republic of Moldova (GoM) is pursuing a policy agenda to support export-led economic growth. In this regard, an improved business environment is essential to foster sustainable private sector growth. Significant regulatory and institutional weaknesses in the business environment have been identified by the recently conducted Investment Climate Assessment as major obstacles to the private sector’s ability to perform efficiently and grow, and they also negatively affect investor confidence. The presence of cumbersome regulations undermines the competitiveness of private Moldovan enterprises and prevents increased investment by increasing the cost of doing business, and ultimately providing fertile ground for corruption, favoritism, and the informal economy.

GoM is currently implementing a project - the Micro, Small, Medium Enterprises (MSME) Competitiveness Project, which takes a comprehensive approach to business competitiveness with funding from the International Development Association and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development.

The MSME’s project development objectives (PDO) are: (i) to reduce the regulatory burden, increase access to finance, increase the export competitiveness of Moldovan enterprises, and (ii) in case of an Eligible Crisis or Emergency, to respond promptly and effectively to it.

The PDO will be achieved through a set of activities that aim to: (a) digitize government-to-business services and inspections, streamline permissive documents, and enhance national quality infrastructure to reduce the regulatory burden enterprises face; (b) support access to finance for enterprises through credit guarantees and enhance the capacity of the Credit Guarantee Fund (CGF), and (c) support the development of MSMEs and enhance their export competitiveness; d) support project management; e) support the government's response in case of an emergency.

 

B.           BACKGROUND OF THE ASSIGNMENT

The target segment of the current assignment is National Quality Infrastructure System (NQI). NQI activities under the project focuses on increasing MSME competitiveness and enabling exports. The NQI activities aim at addressing the enterprise sector’s difficulties in competing in foreign markets caused by the existing gaps in NQI and services. Improving the NQI system will be achieved through: (a) building capacity in metrology and testing area by upgrading selected laboratories and strengthening institutional capacity in order to expand the list of measurements and testing demanded by export oriented firms; (b) ensuring the traceability of the measurements performed to enterprises, as well as access to quality infrastructure services due to increased number of calibrations and accredited cross-comparisons at the European Union (EU) level and (c) strengthening accreditation and certification capacity. 

Investment and technical assistance needs are significantly higher than what the Project can support. Thus, an allocation of approximately US$7 million equivalent will address these priority needs. Special attention will be paid to building skills among specialists to perform measurements and ensure more laboratories and services are accredited meeting the EU requirements.

Within this framework, the Government of Moldova through the Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization (the Client) and the National Metrology Institute (the Beneficiary) are seeking the services of an EURAMET member metrology institute (hereinafter Consultant), who has relevant expertise in the field of the assignment to provide the know-how transfer and training of the specialists of the Moldovan National Metrology Institute (hereinafter NMI).

 

C.           Objectives of the Assignment

The main objectives of the assignment are to enhance the technical competence and knowledge in the field of mass metrology of Moldovan NMI specialists through comprehensive training and structured know-how transfer, focusing on both theoretical knowledge and practical skills in the following domains: (i) Mass measurements; (ii) Length measurements; (iii) Pressure measurements and (iv) Force measurements.

D.           Task to be performed (Scope of Work)

To achieve the assignment’s objectives, the Consultant shall develop the training materials and deliver trainings for NMI specialists at the NMI premises and ensure practical on-site trainings for specialists of NMI at Consultant’ premises according to the topics, duration and timeline suggested below.

TASK I - Mass Measurements

For the topics related to mass measurements, the Consultant will have to:

  • Develop and submit to the Client training materials.
  • Design and deliver training courses (at NMI premises) and practical trainings (at Consultant’ premises) in separate courses on mass measurements as follows:
  1. Advanced Training for Calibrating Standard Weights

Further below a detailed technical composition of the expected training topics is presented.

Application of advanced calibration methods under controlled conditions including:

  • Preparation of weights for calibration;
  • Gravimetric vs. comparative calibration;
  • Choice of equipment and correct handling;
  • Determination of conventional and real mass;
  • Control of external influences (humidity, temperature, pressure).

Correct development of uncertainty budgets according to GUM including:

  • Types of uncertainty: type A and type B;
  • Applied examples of uncertainty budgets;
  • Extended calculation and expression of results;
  • Estimation of individual contributions: equipment, operator, environment.

Ensuring the quality of the calibration process and traceability of results including:

  • Metrological traceability: the traceability chain and national standards;
  • Writing calibration reports;
  • Document archiving, retention and review requirements;
  • Preparation for ISO/IEC 17025 audit.

Applying knowledge in real situations and developing analytical skills including:

  • Complete calibration of a set of weights (practical);
  • Identification and correction of possible errors;
  • Case study: internal audit simulation with technical file analysis.
  • Support of interlaboratory comparison

 

Tentative schedule, duration and number of participants to the theoretical and practical trainings is described below.

Composition of the on-site practical training at Consultant’ premises:

  • 8 hours theory;
  • 19 hours laboratory practice;
  • 10 hours result evaluation and preparation of calibration certificate;
  • 3 hours practical evaluation of knowledge.

Training at NMI premises:

  • 8 hours theory;
  • 16 hours laboratory practice;
  • 12 hours result evaluation and preparation of calibration certificate;
  • 4 hours practical evaluation of knowledge.
  1. Advanced Training for Calibrating Non-Automatic Weighing Instruments

A detailed technical composition of the expected training topics is presented further below.

Application of advanced calibration methods under controlled conditions including:

Complete understanding of the calibration method described in the EURAMET guide cg-18:

  • General test conditions: stability, environment, location;
  • Waiting time, hysteresis effects, loading-unloading;
  • Preliminary checks of the instrument;
  • Determination of indication errors at different loads;
  • Repeatability and eccentricity.

Complete application of a calibration procedure on a real NAWI:

  • Preparation of the device and selection of standard weights;
  • Multi-point calibration: increasing, decreasing loads;
  • Correction of weighing errors;
  • Evaluation of the effect of the weight position on the platform (eccentricity).

Development of the uncertainty budget associated with the calibration of a NAWI:

  • Sources of uncertainty in the calibration of scales: weights, instrument, environmental influences;
  • Structure and completion of an uncertainty budget;
  • Calculation of combined and extended uncertainty;
  • Examples of calculations in Excel.

Ensuring traceability and compliance of technical documentation:

  • Structure and content of a calibration report;
  • Metrological traceability requirements;
  • Reference equipment tracking and related records;
  • Examples of complete calibration reports.

 

Training of personnel for audits and maintaining accreditation:

  • Critical aspects assessed by auditors;
  • Process control and method validation;
  • Non-conformity management and corrective actions.

TASK II- Length Measurements

For the topics related to length measurements, the Consultant will have to:

  • Develop and submit to the Client training materials.
  • Design and deliver theoretical training courses (at NMI premises) and practical trainings (at Consultant’ premises) in separate courses on length measurements as follows:
  1. Training for handling and calibration of gauge blocks, calipers, micrometers and comparators calibration of rulers and tapes

A detailed technical composition of the expected training topics is presented further below.

  • The Normative documentation in the field with requirements and technical aspects
  • Technical and metrology aspects
  • Correct handling of instruments (care and maintenance)
  • Calibration procedures
  • Identification and evaluation of uncertainty factors
  • Determining and calculating uncertainty

Theoretical trainings will be provided in Chisinau within NMI’ facilities. Estimated duration of the all trainings is estimated at 25 days or around 200 academic hours.

 

Practical training (on-site training) will be provided abroad within the Consultant’ laboratory. Each on-site training will be structured for 4-5 days /domain.

 

F.            Common details and requirements for the Consultant’s work

The tasks accomplishment will end at the middle of 2009. The consecutiveness of the task accomplishment is free, at the opinion of the consultant and according the availableness of the trainers and bodies that will be involved in realisation of the project.

Recommended documents, language:

  • All key theoretical training materials, printed documents including Power-Point applications, will be delivered in English. Each participant will receive hand-outs of the related training material. The training materials and document during the trainings will be available in English.
  • The supporting documents should have added value, importance and significance for participants in respect to the objectives described.

The Consultant will have to consider for expenditure estimation inter alia the following items of the costs:

  • Fees for trainers (training in Moldova plus preparation/reporting at home), daily allowance for staying in Moldova;
  • Cost of necessary international and local travel, including transportation of the Personnel of the Consultant by the most appropriate means of transport and the most direct practicable route;
  • Cost of applicable international or local communications such as the use of telephone and email required for the purpose of the Services;
  • Development presentations and supporting documents in English Printing materials;
  • Renting training room (including refreshment);
  • Renting technical equipment (data projector, interpretation facilities);
  • Organization and logistics etc. at place;
  • Fees for laboratory use, if applicable;
  • In-country travel costs for Moldovan specialists during the internships (i.e. airport pick-up and drop, etc);
  • Development presentations and supporting documents in English (internships)

 

The Consultant shall be responsible for:

  • Carrying out the required assessment at best level;
  • Coordination of the progress status with the Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization (MEDD) and PIU for MSME;
  • Producing, for delivery to the MSME PIU and to the Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalization of all specified below deliverables in a timely manner and acceptable quality.

G.           Reports / Deliverables

Within the time frame of this assignment, the Consultant will be expected to develop the following deliverables:

  • First Progress Report. This paper will comprise inter alia (i) theoretical training programs; (ii) training materials by training topic based on training programs and (iii) description and planning how the practical trainings (internships) will be organized, inter alia agenda for the internship. The report will be submitted within four weeks after commencing the assignment.
  • Second Progress Report. This paper will include the report on theoretical training sessions delivered by the Consultant to specialists of NMI. The report will be submitted within eight weeks after commencing the assignment.
  • Third Progress Report. This paper will include the report on practical trainings (internships) provided by the Consultant. The report will be submitted within eleven weeks after commencing the assignment.
  • Final Report. The Final Report is the report comprising all the assignment results. The Report will be submitted within thirteen weeks after commencing the assignment.

The PIU and the MEDD may provide comments to the deliverables, which should be addressed by the Consultant accordingly.

 

All Deliverables will be provided in electronic form and in hard copies (if required). The language of the deliverables shall be English and Romanian.

 

  1. PERIOD and TERMS of the ASSIGNMENT

The assignment will be implemented in the period from May to July, 2026.

 

  1.  Local Inputs

The NMI will provide to the Consultant the following available materials and support:

    • Logistical support relevant to the assignment;
    • Information on type and models of the metrology equipment available within the metrology laboratories of the Client.

 

      1. Requirements for the assignment

This assignment will require an EURAMET metrology institute or consortium such metrology institutes with appropriate technical and metrological qualification, comparable standards and internationally recognized knowledge, which:

  • Has relevant competence in the field of length, mass pressure and force measurements including relevant Calibration and Measurement Capabilities in the Bureau International des Poids et Measures (BIPM) key comparison database.
  • Has demonstrated previous experience in providing similar internship and/or trainings in relevant subject fields.
  • Has experience in the implementation of the donors’ and/or IFI’s sponsored projects.
  • Has experience in preparation of analytical reports, training programs and training curricula.

 

k.           Terms of payment

The Contract will be the Standard World Bank Lump-sum contract.

FEDERAL GOVERNMENT OF NIGERIA

FEDERAL MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES AND SANITATION

SUSTAINABLE POWER AND IRRIGATION FOR NIGERIA (SPIN) PROJECT

IDA Credit No: IDA76370

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST FOR CONSULTANCY SERVICES

Assignment Title: ENGAGEMENT OF A CONSULTING FIRM FOR CONSTRUCTION SUPERVISION OF THE DESIGN & BUILD OF IRRIGATION SCHEMES FOR ADANI (ENUGU STATE) AND NDIEZE (EBONYI STATE) IRRIGATION SCHEME

Reference No.: FMWR&S/SPIN/QCBS/CS/9D

The Federal Government of Nigeria (FGN), through the Federal Ministry of Water Resources and Sanitation (FMWRS), has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of implementing the Sustainable Power and Irrigation for Nigeria (SPIN) Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds to finance the engagement of a Consulting Firm for the Construction Supervision of the Design & Build Irrigation Schemes (Modernization and Expansion) across selected irrigation schemes nationwide.

The SPIN Project is designed to strengthen dam safety and improve the management of water resources for hydropower and irrigation in selected areas of Nigeria. Under Subcomponents 2.2 and 2.3 of the Project, the FGN seeks to rehabilitate and modernize irrigation and drainage infrastructure while improving irrigation management systems to enhance water delivery efficiency, expand command areas, and strengthen climate resilience.

Purpose of the Assignment

The modernization and expansion of the irrigation schemes will be executed under a Design Build (DB) contractual arrangement governed by the FIDIC Yellow Book (2017 Edition). Due to the complexity of the DB modality, the Employer requires an independent and highly qualified Supervision Consultant (“the Consultant”) to act as the Employer’s Representative throughout the project life cycle.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for Adani and Ndieze Irrigation Scheme located in Enugu & Ebonyi States, can be accessed at the following link: https://1drv.ms/w/c/bea66a6a0847ee73/IQBvbJdu_lTLQaK7gY9BbIhQAWl_4w8Ua5FAa1Ayy2NP3PA?e=ANEyvK

The Federal Ministry of Water Resources and Sanitation, through the Federal Project Management Unit (FPMU) of the SPIN Project, now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested firms must provide sufficient information demonstrating that they meet the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

Shortlisting Criteria

  • The firm shall have a minimum of ten (10) years of demonstrated in experience providing construction supervision services for large scale infrastructure projects, Experience with Design Build (DB) or FIDIC Yellow Book based contracts is an added advantage.
  • The firm shall demonstrate experience in the supervision (which includes experience in reviewing, verifying and approving detailed engineering designs during implementation of irrigation schemes/projects, including hydraulic, geotechnical, structural, electromechanical, and SCADA/telemetry systems) of at least three (3) irrigation projects of comparable scale and complexity within the past ten (10) years.
  • The firm shall demonstrate experience in supervising rehabilitation, or expansion of gravity fed and pressurized irrigation systems, including canal networks (open/closed channels), water control structures, drainage systems, and on farm distribution infrastructure.
  • The firm shall demonstrate its technical and managerial capabilities, including the capacity to mobilize a multidisciplinary team of qualified engineers and specialists for the supervision of large irrigation infrastructure projects.

Evidence of similar assignments previously undertaken (Contract Award Letters, Job Completion Letters, and other evidence that may be required to verify such experience).

NOTE: Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

Selection of the Consulting Firm

Consultants will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, 7th Edition (September 2025) (“Procurement Regulations”), and open to all eligible firms as defined therein.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.15, and 3.16 of the Procurement Regulations, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms in the form of a Consortium/Joint Venture to enhance their qualifications and should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a subconsultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all partners shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. Evidence of such association must be provided in the Expression of Interest.

The implementation period for this assignment shall be Twenty-Six (26) months from the date the contract became effective.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in written form to the address below (in person, by mail, or by email) on or before 2:00 p.m. on 28th July, 2026.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. (local time), Monday to Friday.

procnotices.contact_address: Ramalla
procnotices.contact_organization: Ministry of Planning and International Cooperation
procnotices.notice_text:
The Ministry of Finance and Planning (MoFP) is seeking to recruit qualified Data Analysis and Reporting Officer under the Social Recovery & Job Creation Project (SRJC), financed by the World Bank for the benefit of The Ministry of Local Government.

The selected Data Analysis and Reporting Officer will be assigned to work at the Ministry of Local Government — to support the Ministry of Local Government in strengthening institutional reporting, improving data analysis, and enhancing the quality and consistency of information used for planning, monitoring, and decision-making.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Data Analysis and Reporting Officer will support the collection, validation, analysis, and reporting of institutional data and information. The Officer will coordinate with relevant departments to improve reporting processes, prepare analytical reports, and support evidence-based planning and institutional performance.

Main Duties and Responsibilities

  • Collect, organize, validate, and analyze reports and data received from relevant departments.
  • Prepare periodic reports, statistical summaries, analytical reports, briefing notes, and presentations.
  • Coordinate with relevant departments to ensure the timely submission and accuracy of reports and data.
  • Consolidate institutional reports and ensure the consistency and completeness of information.
  • Maintain and update reporting records, databases, and related documentation.
  • Develop dashboards, charts, and reporting tools to support management decision-making.
  • Review data quality and identify inconsistencies or gaps requiring follow-up.
  • Support the preparation of reports required by senior management, development partners, and other stakeholders.
  • Recommend improvements to reporting systems and data analysis practices.
  • Maintain organized electronic and hard-copy records related to reporting and data analysis.
  • Perform any other related duties as may be assigned by the Director General of the Projects Department.

Job Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree from an accredited university in Business Administration, Statistics, Information Systems, Management Information Systems, Economics, Public Administration, or any other related field.
  • Minimum of two (2) years of relevant professional experience in reporting, data analysis, institutional reporting, or administrative coordination.
  • Demonstrated experience in preparing reports, analyzing quantitative and qualitative data, and presenting findings.
  • Experience working with government institutions or internationally financed projects is an advantage.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
  • Experience in Power BI, Excel dashboards, or other data visualization tools is considered an advantage.
  • Excellent communication and report-writing skills in both Arabic and English.
  • Ability to prioritize tasks, meet deadlines, and work effectively under pressure.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team.
