procnotices.notice_text:
FEDERAL GOVERNMENT OF NIGERIA

FEDERAL MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES AND SANITATION

SUSTAINABLE POWER AND IRRIGATION FOR NIGERIA (SPIN) PROJECT

IDA Credit No: IDA76370

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST FOR CONSULTANCY SERVICES

Assignment Title: ENGAGEMENT OF A CONSULTING FIRM FOR CONSTRUCTION SUPERVISION OF THE DESIGN & BUILD OF IRRIGATION SCHEMES AT DOMA & GALALA (NASARAWA AND BAUCHI STATES)

Reference No.: FMWR&S/SPIN/QCBS/CS/9C

The Federal Government of Nigeria (FGN), through the Federal Ministry of Water Resources and Sanitation (FMWRS), has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of implementing the Sustainable Power and Irrigation for Nigeria (SPIN) Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds to finance the engagement of a Consulting Firm for the Construction Supervision of the Design & Build Irrigation Schemes (Modernization and Expansion) across selected irrigation schemes nationwide.

The SPIN Project is designed to strengthen dam safety and improve the management of water resources for hydropower and irrigation in selected areas of Nigeria. Under Subcomponents 2.2 and 2.3 of the Project, the FGN seeks to rehabilitate and modernize irrigation and drainage infrastructure while improving irrigation management systems to enhance water delivery efficiency, expand command areas, and strengthen climate resilience.

Purpose of the Assignment

The modernization and expansion of the irrigation schemes will be executed under a Design Build (DB) contractual arrangement governed by the FIDIC Yellow Book (2017 Edition). Due to the complexity of the DB modality, the Employer requires an independent and highly qualified Supervision Consultant (“the Consultant”) to act as the Employer’s Representative throughout the project life cycle.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for Doma Irrigation Scheme in Nasarawa State and the Galala Irrigation Scheme in Bauchi State can be accessed at the following link: https://1drv.ms/w/c/bea66a6a0847ee73/IQCvbzcjPRliSKbJ9geE45hUAX-q_SEiWfVAQvI22qgTn2c?e=YHKO0p

 

The Federal Ministry of Water Resources and Sanitation, through the Federal Project Management Unit (FPMU) of the SPIN Project, now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested firms must provide sufficient information demonstrating that they meet the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

Shortlisting Criteria

  • The firm shall have a minimum of ten (10) years of demonstrated in experience providing construction supervision services for large scale infrastructure projects, Experience with Design Build (DB) or FIDIC Yellow Book based contracts is an added advantage.
  • The firm shall demonstrate experience in the supervision (which includes experience in reviewing, verifying and approving detailed engineering designs during implementation of irrigation schemes/projects, including hydraulic, geotechnical, structural, electromechanical, and SCADA/telemetry systems) of at least three (3) irrigation projects of comparable scale and complexity within the past ten (10) years.
  • The firm shall demonstrate experience in supervising rehabilitation, or expansion of gravity fed and pressurized irrigation systems, including canal networks (open/closed channels), water control structures, drainage systems, and on farm distribution infrastructure.
  • The firm shall demonstrate its technical and managerial capabilities, including the capacity to mobilize a multidisciplinary team of qualified engineers and specialists for the supervision of large irrigation infrastructure projects.

Evidence of similar assignments previously undertaken (Contract Award Letters, Job Completion Letters, and other evidence that may be required to verify such experience).

NOTE: Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

Selection of the Consulting Firm

Consultants will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, 7th Edition (September 2025) (“Procurement Regulations”), and open to all eligible firms as defined therein.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.15, and 3.16 of the Procurement Regulations, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms in the form of a Consortium/Joint Venture to enhance their qualifications and should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a subconsultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all partners shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. Evidence of such association must be provided in the Expression of Interest.

The implementation period for this assignment shall be Twenty-Six (26) months from the date the contract became effective.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in written form to the address below (in person, by mail, or by email) on or before 2:00 p.m. on 28th August 2026.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. (local time), Monday to Friday.

Republic of Liberia

INFRASTRUCTURE IMPLEMENTATION UNIT

MINISTRY OF PUBLIC WORKS

P. O Box 9011

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

Country:               Liberia

Loan No.:              63590

Project ID:            P149279

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Traffic Count, Origin–Destination, Stated Preference, and Willingness-to-Pay (WTP) Survey for Proposed Toll Highway Corridors in Liberia

Reference No.:  LR-IIU-558965-CS-CQS

  1. The Government of Liberia has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Southeastern Corridor Road Assets Management Project (SECRAMP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consulting Services for traffic count, origin–destination, stated preference, and willingness-to-pay (WTP) surveys for proposed toll highway corridors in Liberia.
  2. The Consulting Services (“the Services”) include but are not limited to conducting surveys along proposed highway toll corridors as described in the ToR. The Ministry of Public Works through its Infrastructure Implementation Unit (IIU) reserves the right to revise, add to, or remove corridors from the proposed list before or during the assignment. The consultant is expected to propose optimal survey station locations along each corridor in the Inception Report, subject to MPW approval. The following surveys, experience, analysis and forecasting are expected to be carried out: (i) Traffic Count Survey, (ii) Origin-Destination Survey, (iii) Stated Preference Surveys and Experiments, (iv) Willingness-to-Pay Analysis, (v) Traffic Demand Forecasting, and (vi) Toll Rate Recommendations
  3. The Infrastructure Implementation Unit of the Ministry of Public Works now invites eligible Consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are a) Core Business and Years in Business, b) Technical Managerial Organization of the Firm, c) Experience in Similar Assignments, d) Experience in Similar Conditions. Key Expert will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

          4. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Procurement in Investment Project Financing, Goods, Works, non-Consulting and Consulting services dated July 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020, September 2023, and September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on Conflict of Interest.

procnotices.bid_description: CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR CONSTRUCTION SUPERVISION OF THE DESIGN AND BUILD WORKS AT KAMPE-OMI IRRIGATION SCHEME IN KOGI STATE AND DUKKU-LADE IRRIGATION SCHEME IN KWARA STATE

procnotices.notice_text:
FEDERAL GOVERNMENT OF NIGERIA

FEDERAL MINISTRY OF WATER RESOURCES AND SANITATION

SUSTAINABLE POWER AND IRRIGATION FOR NIGERIA (SPIN) PROJECT

IDA Credit No: IDA76370

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST FOR CONSULTANCY SERVICES

Assignment Title: ENGAGEMENT OF A CONSULTING FIRM FOR CONSTRUCTION SUPERVISION OF THE DESIGN & BUILD OF IRRIGATION SCHEME AT KAMPE OMI & DUKU LADE (KOGI AND KWARA STATES

Reference No.: FMWR&S/SPIN/QCBS/CS/9C

The Federal Government of Nigeria (FGN), through the Federal Ministry of Water Resources and Sanitation (FMWRS), has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of implementing the Sustainable Power and Irrigation for Nigeria (SPIN) Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds to finance the engagement of a Consulting Firm for the Construction Supervision of the Design & Build Irrigation Schemes (Modernization and Expansion) across selected irrigation schemes nationwide.

The SPIN Project is designed to strengthen dam safety and improve the management of water resources for hydropower and irrigation in selected areas of Nigeria. Under Subcomponents 2.2 and 2.3 of the Project, the FGN seeks to rehabilitate and modernize irrigation and drainage infrastructure while improving irrigation management systems to enhance water delivery efficiency, expand command areas, and strengthen climate resilience.

Purpose of the Assignment

The modernization and expansion of the irrigation schemes will be executed under a Design Build (DB) contractual arrangement governed by the FIDIC Yellow Book (2017 Edition). Due to the complexity of the DB modality, the Employer requires an independent and highly qualified Supervision Consultant (“the Consultant”) to act as the Employer’s Representative throughout the project life cycle.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for Kampe Omi Irrigation Scheme in Kogi State and the Duku Lade Irrigation Scheme in Kwara State: https://1drv.ms/w/c/bea66a6a0847ee73/IQDljU9WIRhJTbNvCe8qjqxSAaaWvFDt36SqLcRCUuaTrU4?e=ztf6Td

The Federal Ministry of Water Resources and Sanitation, through the Federal Project Management Unit (FPMU) of the SPIN Project, now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested firms must provide sufficient information demonstrating that they meet the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

Shortlisting Criteria

  • The firm shall have a minimum of ten (10) years of demonstrated in experience providing construction supervision services for large scale infrastructure projects, Experience with Design Build (DB) or FIDIC Yellow Book based contracts is an added advantage.
  • The firm shall demonstrate experience in the supervision (which includes experience in reviewing, verifying and approving detailed engineering designs during implementation of irrigation schemes/projects, including hydraulic, geotechnical, structural, electromechanical, and SCADA/telemetry systems) of at least three (3) irrigation projects of comparable scale and complexity within the past ten (10) years.
  • The firm shall demonstrate experience in supervising rehabilitation, or expansion of gravity fed and pressurized irrigation systems, including canal networks (open/closed channels), water control structures, drainage systems, and on farm distribution infrastructure.
  • The firm shall demonstrate its technical and managerial capabilities, including the capacity to mobilize a multidisciplinary team of qualified engineers and specialists for the supervision of large irrigation infrastructure projects.

Evidence of similar assignments previously undertaken (Contract Award Letters, Job Completion Letters, and other evidence that may be required to verify such experience).

NOTE: Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

Selection of the Consulting Firm

Consultants will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, 7th Edition (September 2025) (“Procurement Regulations”), and open to all eligible firms as defined therein.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.15, and 3.16 of the Procurement Regulations, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms in the form of a Consortium/Joint Venture to enhance their qualifications and should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a subconsultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all partners shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. Evidence of such association must be provided in the Expression of Interest.

The implementation period for this assignment shall be Twenty-Six (26) months from the date the contract became effective.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in written form to the address below (in person, by mail, or by email) on or before 2:00 p.m. on 28th August 2026.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours, 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. (local time), Monday to Friday.

PROJET DE RENFORCEMENT DE L’ÉDUCATION POUR AMÉLIORER LES RÉSULTATS EN MATIÈRE DE CAPITAL HUMAIN (PREMCH )

Financement Projet N° P507220

                     Don N°E4100-KM

AVIS DE DEMANDE DE COTATION OUVERTE

Date de Publication : 29 Juillet 2026

Madame, Monsieur,

D’une manière générale, l'Union des Comores à travers le Ministère de l’Education Nationale, de l’Enseignement, de la Recherche Scientifique, de la Formation et de l’Insertion Professionnelle s’associe et participe à l’Approche programmatique multi phase (APM) pour promouvoir des méthodes innovantes pour favoriser l’apprentissage en Afrique de l’est et australe. L’APM proposée, intitulée « Advancing Innovative Methods to Promote Learning » (AIM4Learning) ou Favoriser des méthodes innovantes pour promouvoir l’apprentissage, intègre des approches résolument nouvelles pour offrir une meilleure éducation aux élèves.

Cependant, l’Union des Comores a subi ces dernières années des chocs et des perturbations qui ont fortement impacté le système éducatif du pays, accentué les pertes d’apprentissages, les profondes inégalités scolaires et les risques d’exclusion scolaire des groupes les plus vulnérables. Il est nécessaire de rétablir et sauvegarder l’éducation en tant que droit fondamental, vecteur de développement, facteur de réduction de la pauvreté et levier puissant pour la paix, la résilience aux changements climatiques et au développement durable.

C’est ainsi que le Gouvernement comorien a obtenu un Don de l’Association internationale de développement (IDA) et du Fonds du Partenariat mondial pour l’éducation équivalent à 23,7 millions de dollars pour répondre aux besoins du pays en matière d’amélioration et du renforcement de l’éducation pour l’amélioration des Résultats en Matière de Capital Humain aux Comores.

Il est prévu qu’une partie des sommes accordées au titre de ce Don sera utilisée pour effectuer les paiements à titre du contrat portant « Travaux de réhabilitation du local du Responsable insulaire du PREMCH à Mohéli » de l’Union des Comores.

Par la présente, nous invitons votre entreprise à soumettre une offre ferme sous scellé pour les Travaux de réhabilitation du local du Responsable insulaire du PREMCH à Mohéli.

La procédure sera conduite par la mise en concurrence en recourant à une demande de prix telle que définie dans le « Règlement de Passation des Marchés dans le Cadre du Financement de Projets D’investissements (FPI) Fournitures, Travaux, Services Autres que des Services de Consultants et Services de Consultants » 7ème Edition Septembre 2025.

L’offre doit être accompagnée d’une Garantie de soumission d’un montant de 1 600 200 KMF (Un million six cent mille deux cent francs Comoriens) sous forme d’une garantie bancaire ou une compagnie d’assurance ou un chèque de banque.

Les spécifications techniques des travaux nécessaires sont jointes à la présente invitation à soumissionner.

Votre entreprise pourrait obtenir de plus amples informations auprès de la Coordination nationale du PREMCH/PREMCH à l’adresse suivante :

UGP

Coordination nationale

Moroni-Mboueni

Tel : 333 34 54

E -mail : cn@pfss-comores.org

Les offres et toutes les informations requises dans les Instructions aux Soumissionnaires (ci-joint), devront être envoyées l’adresse mentionnée ci-haut et au plus tard le Mercredi 12 août 2026 à 10 h 00.

NB : Votre offre devra être chiffrée toutes taxes, impôts, frais et droits applicables compris, notamment les droits d’enregistrement du marché auprès des administrations compétentes. Le soumissionnaire demeure responsable de la vérification et de l’intégration de l’ensemble de ses obligations fiscales dans les prix proposés.

Les dossiers déposés en retard ne seront pas pris en compte.

Les offres seront ouvertes le jour même à 10h00 à tous soumissionnaires souhaiterons assister.

Les offres devront être valides pour une période de quatre-vingt-dix jours (90 jours) après la date limite de dépôt et ouverture des offres.

Télécharger le dossier de la demande de cotation sur le site du projet: pfss-comores.org

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(Consulting Services – Firms Selection)

Country: Kenya

Project Name: Horn of Africa Gateway Development Project 

Credit No.: 6768-KE

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Feasibility Study and Transaction Advisory Services for the Nairobi – Mombasa Road Under a Public Private Partnership Framework

Reference No.: Tender No.: KeNHA/3002/2026

1. The Government of the Republic of Kenya has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Horn of Africa Gateway Development Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consulting Services.

2. The Consulting Services (“the Services”) include Consultancy Services for Feasibility Study and Transaction Advisory Services for the Nairobi – Mombasa Road under a Public Private Partnership Framework.

3. The period of the Services is fifteen (15) months and shall include six (6) months for Phase 1 - Feasibility Studies and nine (9) months for Phase 2 - Transaction Advisory Services. The estimated number of person-months for key professional personnel for both Phase 1 and Phase 2 is 156 person-months comprising 88 person-months for Feasibility Study Phase and 68 person-months for the Transaction Advisory Services Phase.

The Detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) can be found at the following website: www.kenha.co.ke.

4. The Kenya National Highways Authority, a State Corporation under the Ministry of Roads and Transport established under the Kenya Roads Act, 2007, now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

a) Core Business and Years in Business

The firm(s) shall demonstrate that their core business and principal areas of practice are in: (i) Transportation and highway engineering; (ii) Transport infrastructure planning and advisory; (iii) Engineering feasibility studies; and (iv) Public-Private Partnership (PPP) transaction advisory services; or closely related fields, for a period of at least fifteen (15) years.

b) Relevant experience 

The firm(s) shall demonstrate successful completion of at least three (3) assignments of similar nature, scope, and complexity, undertaken within the last ten (10) years in a comparable operating environment. The assignments shall collectively demonstrate experience in the following areas: (i) Transport infrastructure feasibility studies; (ii) Highway planning and engineering design; (iii) Traffic engineering, transport demand forecasting and Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS); (iii) Environment and Social safeguards studies for transport infrastructure projects; and (iv) PPP Advisory Services including project structuring, financial analysis, procurement support, and transaction management for the selection of private partners.

For each assignment undertaken, the Expression of Interest (EOI) shall provide the following information: (i) Client name and address; (ii) Description of the assignment and scope of services; (iii) Contract value; and (iv) Assignment duration (start and completion dates).

c) Technical and Managerial Capability of the Firm(S) 

The firm(s) shall demonstrate as having the requisite technical capability, which shall entail a description of relevant personnel, equipment, software, etc., and managerial capacity to undertake the assignment.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

Due to the need for brevity, interested Consultants should only provide sufficient information that will enable the Client to determine the Consultant’s capabilities in the field of the assignment. Legal documents such as certificates of incorporations, power of attorney, or translations of standard brochures should not be submitted at this stage.  The maximum page limit for the EOI, including any annexes, shall therefore not exceed thirty (30) pages. This limit applies for single entities as well as firms in associations.

5. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016 revised in September 2025 (7th Edition) (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

6. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. procnotices.notice_text:
REPUBLIC OF ANGOLA

MINISTRY OF PLANNING

ACCELERATING ECONOMIC DIVERSIFICATION AND JOB CREATION PROJECT

Loan No.: IBRD-95270

Project ID: P178035

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

Assignment Title: CONSULTING SERVICE FOR THE DEVELOPMENT AND TECHNICAL, ENVIRONMENTAL, SOCIAL STUDIES, AND ENVIRONMENTAL LICENSING FOR LAST-MILE INFRASTRUCTURE IN HUAMBO, BIÉ AND BENGUELA

Reference No. 95CS2/MINPLAN/26

 

The Government of Angola has received financing from the World Bank Group's International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) toward the cost of the Accelerating Economic Diversification and Job Creation Project (Diversifica Mais) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for the Development and Technical, Environmental, Social Studies, and Environmental Licensing for Last-Mile Infrastructure in Huambo, Bié and Benguela.

Consulting Services (“the Services”) aim to provide technical support to the Ministry of Planning, through the DIVERSIFICA+ Project Implementation Unit (PIU), in all phases prior to the execution of last-mile infrastructure projects in the provinces of Huambo, Bié, and Benguela. The role of the consulting firm includes:

  1. Identifying the technical, economic, and social needs of the selected productive infrastructures, mapping existing site conditions, and inventorying current infrastructure assets in the intervention areas;
  2. Developing technical, economic, and financial feasibility studies for the subprojects, defining engineering and architectural alternatives, and estimating the construction, operation, and maintenance costs;
  3. Preparing preliminary engineering and architectural designs to serve as a robust basis for future detailed design and construction bidding documents;
  4. Preparing Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIA) and associated instruments, verifying compliance with national legislation and World Bank environmental and social standards, and validating proposed mitigation measures;
  5. Evaluating the national legal and regulatory framework relevant to land use, environmental licensing, and infrastructure development, identifying potential bottlenecks or risks, and providing advice and support to the PIU to address them;
  6. Preparing detailed preliminary technical specifications for the core infrastructure modules, covering civil works, solar photovoltaic energy, irrigation systems, and rural road rehabilitation, ensuring technical viability, climate resilience, and sustainability.

 

The expected duration of the consultancy contract will be 5 months.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below.

The Accelerating Economic Diversification and Job Creation Project (Diversifica Mais) now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

  • Possess a minimum of 7 (seven) years of proven experience in preparing technical and economic feasibility studies and in developing preliminary projects for small and medium-scale infrastructure, preferably in the sectors of photovoltaic solar energy, irrigation systems, hydraulic ditches, rural access roads and rehabilitation of small road infrastructure;
  • Possess a minimum of 05 (five) years of proven experience in the preparation of environmental and social studies for infrastructure projects (including ESMPs and other applicable E&S instruments, proportionate to the risk and defined by subproject.), preferably in the sectors of photovoltaic solar energy, irrigation systems, hydraulic ditches, rural access roads and rehabilitation of small road infrastructures
  • Having performed at least 2 (two) tasks of a similar nature in the last 10 (ten) years, involving technical studies or preliminary projects for infrastructure to support local or productive development;
  • Proven experience in carrying out at least two (2) similar projects in Angola or comparable Portuguese-speaking countries, including knowledge of Presidential Decree No. 117/20 and applicable environmental licensing procedures, and involving environmental and social studies of projects and infrastructure to support local or productive development.
  • Demonstrate proven practical experience in preparing cost-benefit analyses, financial modeling, risk assessment, and market studies, including the development of sensitivity scenarios;
  • Demonstrate knowledge and experience in applying the standards and procedures of international financial institutions, namely the World Bank or equivalent multilateral entities, including requirements related to environmental and social safeguards, institutional analysis, and regulatory framework;
  • To demonstrate institutional capacity to operate effectively in multi-stakeholder contexts, ensuring strong technical coordination with public institutions, local authorities, and other relevant actors in Angola, while fostering meaningful engagement with local communities.
  • Possess a valid Environmental Consultancy certification issued by the Ministry of the Environment (MINAMB), proving your legal authorization to conduct environmental studies in Angola. The certification must be presented as part of the Technical Proposal and must be up-to-date at the time of submission.
  • Having established internal quality management and occupational health and safety systems, preferably certified according to ISO 9001 and ISO 45001 standards, or equivalent, will be considered an advantage.

 

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” revised in September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 0800 to 1600 hours.

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (only by mail) until August 27, 2026.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

Lebanese Republic

Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR)

GREEN, AGRI-FOOD TRANSFORMATION FOR ECONOMIC RECOVERY (GATE)

 

Reference :             GC2C2d

Assignment Title:      Detailed Designs, Tender Documents and Supervision of Solid Waste Management Facilities

 

The Republic of Lebanon (the “Borrower”) represented by the Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR) (the “Client”) as a representative to the Borrower will implement the Green, Agri-food Transformation for Economic Recovery (the “GATE” or “Project”), funded by the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (the “IBRD” or the “World Bank” or the “Bank”). The total Project cost is Two Hundred Million United States Dollars (US$ 200,000,000).

The CDR intends to apply a portion of the proceeds of this loan to eligible payments under a consulting services contract for the “Detailed Designs, Tender Documents and Supervision of Solid Waste Management Facilities (GC2C2d)”.

The full TOR version can be found on CDR website www.cdr.gov.lb, click on the Procurement tag for more info.

The Main objective of this assignment is the provision of Engineering/Consulting Services needed for the implementation of the following activities (additional details about each phase are provided in the TOR):

Phase 1: Design services for the construction and/or upgrade of SW infrastructure. These could vary from assessing needs of existing facilities and developing refurbishment and expansion plans, construction of new facilities (sorting, composting and landfills), improvement to the management of existing landfills (expansion, leachate and gas management) and Preparation of Tender Documents and assistance during the tendering stage.

Phase 2: Supervision services for the construction and/or upgrade of SW infrastructure whose design and tender documents have been prepared under phases 1 and 2.

The Engineering/ Consulting firm shall perform the assignments in a manner that would fully attain and fulfil the objectives and outcomes described in the TOR.

The time for completion of the Contract (GC2C2d) is:

For Phase 1: 12 months from the Contract Notification Date.

For Phase 2, 18 months from the Notice to Commence of the construction contractor, plus a defect liability period of 12 months.

The CDR now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services.

Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (brochures, description of similar assignments, experience in similar conditions, availability of appropriate skills among staff, etc.), in a responsive way to the below noted requirements.

In addition, interested consultants are requested to provide the following information, in a binder, and in the same order as listed below, and shall use and fill-in the attached Consultant Information Form, and submit it in one hard copy and one editable (Excel or Word format) soft copy in:

  • A duly completed Cover Letter stating the interest of the applicant in providing the mentioned services.
  • A concise presentation of the firm(s) (brochures, statements of type, property and key tasks etc.).
  • List of ONLY relevant similar projects (maximum 10 projects) as defined in the Terms of References, ongoing and/or completed within the last 10 years, indicating the provided services, the percentage of participation in JV (if any), and the size/value of relevant contracts (in USD and in person-month).
  • Detailed descriptions of two (2) handled completed projects within the last ten (10) years that demonstrate experience in providing design and/or supervision services similar in nature, scope and complexity to the proposed assignment, as defined in the Terms of References, only projects completed within the last ten (10) years shall be considered.
  • Overall firm's employees list and personnel availability and structure (list, number, organization structure, etc… of the core, backstopping and supporting staff).
  • Experience in Lebanon and/or the Middle East.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.13, 3.15 and 3.16 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Sixth Edition, February 2025”, which set forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with another firm in the form of a "Joint Venture" to enhance their qualifications, name and nationality of the partner in charge shall be specified. All members should have well defined inputs to the assignment, and shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire consultant's obligations under the contract.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based Selection method set out in the Procurement Regulations. Eligible firms, which have submitted the necessary statements in a satisfactory responsive way, might be short listed.

 

The shortlisting criteria for firms interested in providing these services include:

  • Core Business and Years of Experience: The firm should have at least 10 years of experience in delivering management, technical, procurement, and monitoring support for comparable-scale solid waste infrastructure projects, including those funded by the World Bank or other development finance institutions (DFIs).
  • Relevant Project Experience: The firm should demonstrate a successful track record in detailed design and/or supervision for the construction and/or upgrade of solid waste infrastructure, including in developing economies.
  • Technical and Managerial Capacity: The firm should have a proven capacity to manage complex, multidisciplinary teams and to deliver projects meeting international standards, especially regarding technical quality, cost control, scheduling, risk management including environmental and social risks.

 

Key experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

REQUEST OF EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (REOI)

CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION

ANGOLA

TERTIARY EDUCATION, SCIENCE, AND TECHNOLOGY PROJECT (TEST)

Loan No.: BIRD 9617-AO

GRANT NO.: TF0C4962-AO

Project ID N.º P179154

DEVELOPMENT OF NATIONAL REFERENCE INSTRUMENTS FOR THE DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION OF HIGHER EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS

REFERENCE NO.:  57/CS/C2SC3.A18.3/26

The Government of the Republic of Angola received a loan of US$150 million from the World Bank (WB) and a donation of US$50 million from the Global Partnership for Education for the implementation of the Tertiary Education, Science, and Technology Project (TEST) and intends to apply part of this financing to hire a firm to provide Development of National Reference Instruments for the Digital Transformation of Higher Education Institutions.

The TEST Project aims to: (i) improve the quality of student preparation to increase total enrolment and expand opportunities for more equitable access; (ii) improve the quality and alignment of curricula with the labour market and instruction in priority training areas; and (iii) improve the governance and management of the education sector.

This consultancy aims the specialized consultancy to support MESCTI in the drafting, validation, consolidation, and preparation for institutional approval of National Reference Instruments for the Digital Transformation of Higher Education Institutions (HEIs).

The consulting service will have a maximum duration of six (6) months.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the email address given below.

The Tertiary Education, Science and Technology Project (TEST) of the Ministry of Tertiary Education, Science, Technology and Innovation now invites eligible consulting Firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The shortlisting criteria are:

The company must demonstrate that it has the following qualifications:

  • The firm must demonstrate prior experience in developing strategic instruments, frameworks, standards, guidelines, or studies related to digital transformation, preferably within the education or public administration sectors;
  • Experience in Sub-Saharan Africa and PALOP contexts will be considered an asset, as will knowledge of international frameworks and best practices applicable to higher education;
  • The firm must present a detailed methodology for the execution of the work, demonstrating the technical capacity for the integrated development of the instruments outlined in the Terms of Reference (ToR).

The consulting firm shall propose a multidisciplinary team with proven qualifications and experience in digital transformation, interoperability, digital governance, higher education, information technology, and digital policies.

 Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” published in September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest: The aforementioned document can be consulted at the following link: http://pubdocs.worldbank.org/en/813421487104372186/Procurement-Regulations-for-IPF-Borrowers-portuguese.pdf

Firms may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

As per the Financing Agreement between the Government of Angola and the World Bank, the Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 8H00 – 15H30.

Expressions of interest must be delivered to the address below by e-mail on October 6th, 2026 at 15:30 (Angola local time).

REPUBLIC OF GHANA

MINISTRY OF ROADS AND HIGHWAYS

DEPARTMENT OF FEEDER ROADS

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES - FIRMS SELECTION)

 

COUNTRY: GHANA

 

NAME OF PROJECT: GHANA MARKET ACCESS AND CONNECTIVITY PROJECT (GMACP)

Project ID No.: P513708

No.

Assignment Titles

Procurement Plan Ref Number

1

Cluster 1B: Consulting Services for Design Review, Construction Supervision and Service Level Maintenance Contract Supervision for Savannah (North Gonja), Upper West and Northern Regions in Ghana

GH-DFR-563281-CS-QCBS

 

  1. The Government of the Republic of Ghana has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Ghana Market Access and Connectivity Project (GMACP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for the four (4) separate assignments: Cluster 1A (Consulting Services for Design Review, Construction Supervision and Service Level Maintenance Contract Supervision for Savannah Region in Ghana); Cluster 1B (Consulting Services for Design Review, Construction Supervision and Service Level Maintenance Contract Supervision for Savannah (North Gonja), Upper West and Northern Regions in Ghana); Cluster 2A (Consulting Services for Design Review, Construction Supervision and Service Level Maintenance Contract Supervision for Oti and Volta (Hohoe and Kpando) Regions in Ghana) and Cluster 2B (Consulting Services for Design Review, Construction Supervision and Service Level Maintenance Contract Supervision for Volta and Eastern (Asuogyaman) Regions in Ghana).

This REOI is for the above-mentioned Cluster 1B.

The primary objective of this assignment is to ensure that all civil works and maintenance services are executed in full compliance with approved designs, technical specifications, contract conditions, environmental and social safeguards, World Bank Environmental, Health, and Safety (EHS) Guidelines and all other applicable World Bank requirements.

2. The consulting services (“the Services”) include the following among others:

i. Review of detailed designs and related documents for the various lots in cluster 1B.

ii. Supervision of the various groups of road lots in cluster 1B

iii. Monitoring during the defect liability period of the constructed roads.

iv. Supervision of service-level maintenance contracts for the respective constructed roads by the client in cluster 1B.

The implementation period and estimated level of effort (professional person-months) for Key Staff for the assignments is as detailed below:

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained by sending an official request to the email addresses given below.

Main E-mail address: elormnyoagbe@icloud.com

Cc: cynthia.anane@mrh.gov.gh, excelgh@yahoo.com

 

3. Eligibility Requirement for the Assignment

The Ministry of Roads and Highways (MRH), acting through the Department of Feeder Roads, now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

(a) Minimum Mandatory Requirements (pass/fail):

  1. Core business in providing consulting services for road infrastructure projects, including design, supervision, and performance-based maintenance management.
  2. Minimum of ten (10) years of continuous business in providing consulting services for road infrastructure projects, including design, supervision, and maintenance management.
  3. Evidence of experience in at least three (3) road infrastructure consulting assignments of similar scope and complexity (design/design review and construction supervision) completed within the last ten (10) years.
  4. Evidence of experience in at least one (1) road infrastructure consulting assignment of similar scope and complexity (performance-based maintenance management) completed within the last ten (10) years.
  5. Demonstrate prior experience and knowledge in applying FIDIC Conditions of Contract.
  6. Experience in applying good Environmental and Social standards and practices to project management and supervision. Experience and knowledge of the Multilateral Development Banks’ Environmental and Social Framework(s) (ESF), including Environmental, Health, and Safety (EHS) Guidelines, Gender-Based Violence (GBV), Sexual Exploitation and Abuse/Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH) prevention and response requirements.

(b) Desirable qualifications and experience (added advantages):

- Experience working in Sub-Saharan Africa, given the specific geographical, climatic, and social contexts.

- Experience with World Bank-funded or other multilateral/bilateral development bank-funded projects.

 

 Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, the Seventh (7th) Edition, September 2025 (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. The Joint Venture/Sub-consultancy agreement or letter of intent to form a joint venture/a sub-consultancy association signed by every participating member shall be submitted with the Expression of Interest (EOI).

 

4. Submission of Expression of Interest

Interested firms must organize their Expression of Interest in the following order:

Chapter 1

  1. Company Profile
  2. Legal Status (Certificate of Incorporation)
  3. Letter of intent or Agreement to form a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy
  4. Organizational chart, a list of Board of Directors, and beneficial ownership.

Chapter 2

  1. Evidence of experience in at least three (3) road infrastructure consulting assignments of similar scope and complexity (design/design review and construction supervision) completed within the last ten (10) years.
  2. Evidence of experience in at least one (1) road infrastructure consulting assignment of similar scope and complexity (performance-based maintenance management) completed within the last ten (10) years.
  3. A summary of assignments undertaken in Sub-Saharan Africa given the specific geographical, climatic, and social contexts, giving the client’s name and the year in which the assignment was carried out

Chapter 3

  1. Experience in World Bank-funded or other multilateral/bilateral development bank-funded projects.
  2. Experience in applying good Environmental and Social standards and practices to project management and supervision, and in assignments involving Multilateral Development Banks’  Environmental and Social Framework(s) (ESF), including Environmental, Health, and Safety (EHS) Guidelines, Gender-Based Violence (GBV), Sexual Exploitation and Abuse/Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH) prevention and response requirements.

The document must be properly paged, and a table of contents provided.

Consultants will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 0900 to 1700 hours GMT.

Expressions of interest dossiers should be clearly marked “Cluster 1B: Consulting Services for Design Review, Construction Supervision and Service Level Maintenance Contract Supervision for Savannah (North Gonja), Upper West and Northern Regions in Ghana” and delivered as an original and three (3) hard copies. In addition, a PDF soft copy must be delivered to the address below (in person or by email) by 16:00 hours GMT on 11th September 2026.

ESWATINI ELECTRICITY COMPANY

 

 

 

 

Request for Expression of Interest (REOI)

Request for Expression of Interest (REOI)

 

Eswatini Electricity Company (EEC)

(Government of the Kingdom of Eswatini)

Consultancy Services for the Feasibility Study for Ngwempisi Multipurpose Hydro Scheme

 

First date of publication:           10 August 2026

Country:                                      Kingdom of Eswatini

Name of Project:                        Accelerating Sustainable and Clean Energy Access Transformation in Eswatini (ASCENT Eswatini) Project

Sector:                                          Energy Sector

Project ID No.:                            P508960

Reference:                                   SZ-ECC-561181-CS-QCBS

Assignment Title:                       Consultancy Services for the Feasibility Study for Ngwempisi Multipurpose Hydro Scheme

 

  1. The Government of the Kingdom of Eswatini (GoKE) has received financing from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD), the International Development Agency (IDA) and grant funding from the Global Public Good (GPG) Facility, which are all under the World Bank. The received financing is for the purposes of implementing the Accelerating Sustainable and Clean Energy Access Transformation in Eswatini (ASCENT Eswatini) Project (P508960) (the Project), with the involvement of the Ministry of Natural Resources and Energy, as set out in the Loan Agreement, Financing Agreement, Grant Agreement and Project Agreements.

 

  1. The EEC now invites Expressions of Interest (EOI) from interested and eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to provide consulting services for the Feasibility Study for Ngwempisi Multipurpose Hydro Scheme.

 

  1. The Consultant shall undertake, but not necessarily be limited to the following tasks:

 

  1. Compilation and Initial Review of Existing Documents and Data

The Consultant shall undertake a highlevel reconnaissance by collecting and reviewing existing reports, data, and policies on the Ngwempisi River and regional strategies, then synthesizing information on institutions, infrastructure, hydrology, geology, environment, and socioeconomic conditions, with further details provided in the Terms of Reference.

 

  1. Review of the Pre-feasibility Study of the Ngwempisi Hydropower Cascading Scheme.

The Consultant shall review the 2018 prefeasibility study to identify gaps for further analysis and update assumptions, including assessment of dam alternatives, type options, and storage capacity, with further details provided in the Terms of Reference.

 

  1. Water resources availability and water demand assessment

The Consultant shall conduct a highlevel assessment of water resources availability and future demands, including climate change impacts, water balance forecasting, and evaluation of storage structures and consumptive uses, with further details provided in the Terms of Reference.

 

  1. Preliminary Studies for Agriculture

The Consultant shall conduct a highlevel assessment of irrigation potential along the Ngwempisi River downstream, including policy review, land and soil suitability, farming systems, value chains, irrigation scheme options, cropping systems, and water demand projections, with further details provided in the Terms of Reference.

 

  1. Environmental and Social Impacts Assessment (ESIA) studies

The Consultant shall conduct a preliminary Environmental and Social Impact Assessment of the project including a Preliminary Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP).

 

  1. Preliminary Cost Estimates, Economic Analysis and Ranking

The Consultant shall conduct a highlevel cost and economic assessment of the preliminary scheme layout, including infrastructure requirements, lifecycle cost comparisons for power production, detailed capital cost breakdowns, and preliminary financial and economic analyses, with further details provided in the Terms of Reference.

 

  1. Assessment of Financing Options

The Consultant shall conduct a highlevel assessment of financing options for the multipurpose water project, considering government fiscal capacity, potential loans from multilateral development banks, and publicprivate partnership arrangements.

 

  1. Preliminary Designs

The Consultant shall prepare highlevel preliminary designs to meet projected needs through 2050, optimizing infrastructure dimensions and capacity to balance water supply, hydropower, irrigation, and environmental flows, while respecting socioenvironmental constraints and international transboundary agreements, with further details provided in the Terms of Reference.

 

  1. Interested consultants must provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform all the services. The following documents shall also be submitted along with the EOI applications by all the consulting firms, including each member of JV firms:
      • Copies of certificates of incorporation/registration of the consulting firms
      • Annual Financial records of the firm(s) for the past 5 years
      • Corporate profile of the firm(s) with quality assurance plan, e.g. ISO 9001, information on organizational strength (Organization structure, number of permanent professional staff and their expertise, qualifications and number of total staff), availability of licensed software and tools.  

 

  1. The qualifications and shortlisting criteria are:
      • At least ten (10) years’ of demonstrated experience in undertaking consultancy services of a similar nature and complexity.
      • Demonstrated experience of at least two (2) relevant assignments involving water resources planning, hydropower, multipurpose dam development, irrigation, environmental and social assessment, feasibility or prefeasibility studies, economic analysis or related infrastructure advisory services.
      • Demonstrated experience of at least one (1) relevant assignment in Africa involving water resources planning, hydropower, multipurpose dam development, irrigation, environmental and social assessment, feasibility or prefeasibility studies, economic analysis or related infrastructure advisory services.
      • Demonstrated experience of at least one (1) relevant assignment in hydropower development, specifically in planning and delivering projects that enhance electricity generation through the establishment of hydropower plants.
      • Demonstrated experience of at least one (1) multidisciplinary studies covering technical, environmental, social, economic, financial, and institutional aspects of infrastructure.

 

  1. The purpose of this EOI is to establish a shortlist of not more than eight (8) Prequalified Respondents for the subsequent Request for Proposal and to invite technical and financial proposals from these Respondents. All responses shall be assessed for completeness. The qualification criteria in (v) above shall be assessed on a Yes/No basis to determine a PASS or FAIL result. Respondents who attain a Pass shall be shortlisted on the following weighted aspects:
  • General Corporate experience in undertaking consultancy services.[10]
  • Specific experience in hydropower development, specifically in planning and delivering projects that enhance electricity generation through the establishment of hydropower plants.[25]
  • Specific experience in multidisciplinary studies covering technical, environmental, social, economic, financial and institutional aspects of infrastructure development.[20]
  • Specific experience in assignments involving water resources planning, hydropower, multipurpose dam development, irrigation, environmental and social assessment, feasibility or prefeasibility studies, economic analysis or related infrastructure advisory services[30]
  • Regional (African) experience in assignments involving water resources planning, hydropower, multipurpose dam development, irrigation, environmental and social assessment, feasibility or prefeasibility studies, economic analysis or related infrastructure advisory services.[15]

 

 

  1. In order to substantiate the aforementioned consulting jobs/contracts, the Consultant shall submit the Completion Certificates or End User Certificate from clients depicting description of services provided. All Completion Certificate or End User Certificates should be in English; Completion Certificates/ End User Certificates in other languages should be translated and notarized. Incomplete Consulting Contracts will not be taken into account and hence will not be evaluated.

 

  1. Consultants may associate with other consultants to enhance their qualifications. For a JV/consortium, the qualifications and experience of the members may be combined to meet the qualification requirements. The Lead Partner shall demonstrate substantial relevant experience and shall be responsible for contract performance. Consortium members may combine qualifications and experience to meet the overall qualification requirements.

 

  1. All submittals from the consulting firms shall be in English language.

 

  1. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.15 to 3.16 of the Seventh edition of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers dated September 2025, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

 

  1. The Consultant(s) shall be evaluated and shortlisted based on the qualifications, experience and capability. Qualifications and Experience of key personnel will not be evaluated at this stage. Shortlisted Consultants will subsequently be invited to submit Technical and Financial Proposals and Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost Based (QCBS) selection method as per the Seventh edition of Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers dated September 2025.
  2. Interested eligible consultants may obtain further information by sending an email to the address below or visiting during office hours from 10.00 to 16.00 hrs. The Terms of Reference for the proposed consulting services can be accessed on the link: https://www.eec.co.sz/electricity/projects/ascent/docs/TERMS_OF_REFERENCE_NGWEMPISI_MULTIPURPOSE_HYDROSCHEME_PRE_FEASIBILITY_STUDY.pdf

 

  1. Expression of interest must be delivered in a written form (in person or by e-mail) to the address below no later than 11h00 SAST on 01 September 2026

 

The Procurement Manager

ASCENT Eswatini Project

Eswatini Electricity Company

Composante 1 - Améliorer l’accès aux prestations monétaires de l’ASD et leur gestion

Financement

Banque mondiale

Acheteur

Agence Nationale du Soutien Social (ANSS)

Référence STEP

MA-ANSS-560929-GO-RFQ

DATE LIMITE DE REMISE ET OUVERTURE DES COTATIONS 01 Sept 2026 à 9h30 (heure du Maroc)

 

Le Gouvernement du Royaume du Maroc a obtenu de la Banque mondiale un prêt destiné au financement du projet « Appui au renforcement des filets sociaux pour le développement humain au Maroc ». Une partie de ce financement sera utilisée pour effectuer financer l’amélioration de l’accès aux prestations monétaires de l’ASD et leur gestion. Dans ce contexte, L’Agence Nationale du Soutien Social invite les fournisseurs admissibles et qualifiés à présenter une cotation pour les fournitures et services connexes décrits ci-après. La procédure est conduite suivant la méthode de Demande de Cotations prévue au Règlement de passation des marchés de la Banque mondiale.

1. Objet et consistance de la demande de cotations

La consultation porte sur l’extension de la plateforme principale du système d’information de l’ANSS. Elle comprend les fournitures suivantes, ainsi que leur installation, leur configuration et leur intégration dans l’environnement existant :

N°

Fourniture

Quantité

Principales exigences

1

Extension de la mémoire du cluster hyperconvergé existant composé de quatre nœuds

32 unités

Barrettes de 64 Go DDR5 (4800 MHz), soit 512 Go additionnels par nœud ; installation et paramétrage du cluster inclus.

2

Extension du stockage SSD NVMe du cluster hyperconvergé

8 unités

Disques SSD NVMe de 7,68 To, à raison de deux disques par nœud ; installation, configuration, intégration et paramétrage inclus.

3

Licence Nutanix Kubernetes Platform (NKP) - Ultimate Edition

1 licence

Souscription pour un cluster de quatre nœuds et une capacité totale de 50 cœurs CPU, avec support éditeur pendant trois ans ; installation et configuration incluses.

Les services connexes comprennent notamment le cadrage du projet, la livraison, l’installation, la configuration, l’intégration et la mise en production, les tests de validation, un audit de sécurité, la formation officielle à la plateforme NKP au profit de quatre agents de l’ANSS, le transfert de compétences et la remise des livrables techniques. Le détail de la prestation est téléchargeable à partir du portail des marchés publics à l’adresse : www.marchespublics.gov.ma.

2.  Lieu d’exécution : Rabat.

3. Délai d’exécution : deux mois et demi (2,5 mois), à compter de l’ordre de service prescrivant le commencement de l’exécution.

4. Garantie : trois (3) années à compter de la réception provisoire.

5. Retrait du dossier et demandes d’éclaircissements

Le dossier de la demande de cotation, est téléchargeable à partir du portail des marchés publics à l’adresse : www.marchespublics.gov.ma.

Les demandes d’éclaircissements doivent être transmises au maître d’ouvrage via le portail marocain des marchés publics  au plus tard le 21 août 2026.

6. Qualification de soumission

Peuvent participer à la présente consultation les sociétés ou personnes physiques légalement constituées et habilitées, dont l’activité couvre la fourniture, l’installation, la configuration et l’intégration des équipements, logiciels informatiques et services connexes objet de la consultation.

Les soumissionnaires doivent :

  • Être admissibles conformément aux règles de la Banque mondiale ;
  • Justifier d’au moins deux références similaires réalisées au cours des cinq dernières années, pour un montant total supérieur ou égale à 1 500 000 DH TTC  pour chaque référence; portant sur des prestations se rapprochant de l’objet de la présente demande de cotation ou leurs copies certifiées conformes à l’original délivrées par les maîtres d’ouvrage publics ou privés, ou par les hommes de l'art sous la direction desquels le concurrent a exécuté des prestations dans le domaine d’installation et d’extension des plateformes des systèmes d’information.

Il est impératif que ces attestations concernent des projets réalisés au cours des cinq dernières années et portent sur des prestations avec un montant total supérieur ou égale à un million cinq cent mille dirhams toutes taxes comprises 1 500 000 DH TTC

  • Signaler toute situation réelle, potentielle ou apparente de conflit d’intérêts ;
  • Ne pas se trouver dans une situation susceptible de compromettre leur capacité à exécuter le marché de manière indépendante, notamment en raison d’obligations présentes ou passées envers d’autres clients ;
  • Ne pas faire l’objet d’une sanction en vigueur prononcée par la Banque mondiale.

 

7. Composition du dossier de la soumission :

  1. Au moins deux attestations de référence similaires à l’objet de la cotation, réalisées au cours des cinq dernières années, pour un montant total de 1 500 000 DH TTC chacune comme spécifié dans le point précédent;
  2. Formulaire de cotation et bordereau des prix et quantités, dûment renseignés, signés et cacheté par la personne habilitée à représenter le concurrent avec indication du prix total (Annexe 1) ;
  3. Tableau de conformité technique dûment renseigné, signé et cacheté par la personne habilitée (Annexe2)
  4. Prospectus et fiches techniques cacheté et signé par la personne habilitée ;
  5. Attestation du constructeur ou de l’éditeur faisant référence à la présente consultation et précisant le niveau de partenariat ;
  6. Les pièces justifiant les pouvoirs conférés à la personne agissant au nom du concurrent ;
  7. Déclaration d’acceptation des Directives de la Banque Mondiale en matière de lutte contre la corruption, et de son régime de sanctions signés et cacheté (Annexe 3) ;
  8. Garantie de soumission en dirhams ou dans une monnaie convertible, sous forme d’une caution bancaire d’un montant de 25 000,00 dirhams en faveur de l’ANSS indiquant l’objet de la cotation.
  9.  Une attestation ou sa copie certifiée conforme à l’original, délivrée depuis moins d’un an par le

percepteur du lieu d’imposition certifiant que le concurrent est en situation fiscale régulière ou

à défaut de paiement qu’il a constitué les garanties. Cette attestation doit mentionner l’activité

au titre de laquelle le concurrent est imposé ;

  1.  Une attestation ou sa copie certifiée conforme à l’original délivrée depuis moins d’un an par la caisse nationale de sécurité sociale ou par tout autre organisme de prévoyance sociale certifiant que le concurrent est en situation régulière envers l’organisme concerné ;

 

Modèles obligatoires : le dossier téléchargeable à partir du portail des marchés publics à l’adresse : www.marchespublics.gov.ma  contient les modèles du formulaire de cotation, du bordereau des prix et quantités, du tableau de conformité technique, de la déclaration d’acceptation des Directives de la banque mondiale anticorruption. Les soumissionnaires doivent utiliser ces modèles sans en modifier la substance.

8. Présentation, signature et validité des cotations

Les concurrents doivent déposer leurs dossiers par voie électronique dans le portail des marchés publics accessible à l'adresse www.marchespublics.gov.ma. Le contenu, la présentation ainsi que le dépôt des dossiers des concurrents doivent être conformes aux dispositions du point 9 au niveau du chapitre I Instruction aux soumissionnaire au niveau du dossier de la demande de cotation téléchargeable à l’adresse www.marchespublics.gov.ma

9. Remise et ouverture des cotations

Le Mardi 1 Septembre 2026, à neuf heures et trente minute (9h30) du matin, il sera procédé dans la salle de réunion du siège de l’Agence Nationale du Soutien social (ANSS) sise à 3, angle Mehdi Ben Barka, bâtiment Millennium Business Center - Souissi, Rabat, Maroc - Rabat, à l’ouverture des plis concernant la demande de cotation numéro prix N° MA-ANSS-563718-GO-RFQ, relatif à l’ Acquisition, installation et mise en service de fournitures matérielles et logicielles destinées au renforcement de l’infrastructure SI de l’Agence Nationale du Soutien Social (ANSS) en présence des représentants des soumissionnaires qui souhaitent

10. Évaluation et attribution

L’évaluation portera successivement sur la qualification du soumissionnaire, la conformité administrative et technique de la cotation, puis sur la vérification arithmétique et la comparaison des prix. Le contrat sera attribué au soumissionnaire admissible et qualifié dont la cotation est conforme aux exigences du dossier et présente le prix évalué le plus bas, selon les critères et la méthode précisés dans le dossier de la demande de cotations.

RNA Extraction Kits, DNA Extraction Kits, PCR Master Mix, SYBR Green RT-PCR Kit, HiScript II One Step qRT-PCR Probe Kit, All-Powerful Multiple Probe qPCR PreMix, PCR Product Sequencing, DNA Library Preparation Kits (Metagenomic Sequencing and Analysis), RNA Library Preparation Kits (Metatranscriptomic Sequencing and Analysis), Primer Synthesis, Absolute Ethanol, 75% Ethanol, 84 Disinfectant Solution, 20 μL Filter Tips, 10 μL Filter Tips, 0.2 mL Centrifuge Tubes, 8-Strip Fluorescence Quantitative PCR Tubes, 50 mL Centrifuge Tubes, 1.5 mL Centrifuge Tube Racks, 50 mL Centrifuge Tube Racks, Hank’s Balanced Salt Solution (HBSS), DEPC-treated Water, 1× PBS Buffer, TS-GelRed Nucleic Acid Gel Stain (10,000× Aqueous Solution), and DNA Marker (2000 bp).

3You may submit a quotation for the above Contract Package in its entirety (partial quotations are not permitted). The Purchaser will evaluate the Goods in accordance with the evaluation criteria specified in the Request for Quotations (RFQ). The Quoter offering the lowest evaluated price among those quotations that substantially meet the requirements shall be selected as the successful Quoter for the Contract Package.

Eligible Quoters:

3.2 Have appropriately qualified technical personnel and the capacity to supply the Goods and provide after-sales services.

Room 1817, 18th Floor, Building 59, Middle Section of East Third Ring Road, Chaoyang District, Beijing, China.

The Republic of Uzbekistan has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the “Innovative Social Protection System for Inclusion of Vulnerable Populations” (INSON) project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include the development, implementation, and delivery of a fully functional Minimum Viable Product (MVP) enabling digital monitoring of all five categories of activities of the “Inson” Centers. The MVP will include:

  • Mobile application for social workers
  • Web panels for social workers, supervisors and operators
  • KPI platform
  • Tracking platform
  • ERP components
  • CRM components
  • Situational management platform
  • Document workflow platform
  • Task management platform
  • Monitoring platform

Estimated level of effort: approximately 4 professional staff-months.

Implementation period: approximately 4 months from contract start.

Expected start date: upon contract signature (tentatively September 2026).

Education and Professional Background

Minimum 5 years in full-stack or mobile development, including relevant experience in:

  • developing mobile applications with GPS, offline mode, and media uploads;

Relevant technical skills include:

  • Frontend: React / Vue / Angular;
  • Mobile: Flutter / Kotlin / React Native;
  • Backend: Node.js / Python / Java / .NET;
  • Databases: PostgreSQL / MySQL;
  • Architectures: REST API, microservices (optional); DevOps: Docker, CI/CD; data security practices.

  • strong communication and documentation skills;

REPUBLIC OF GHANA

MINISTRY OF ROADS AND HIGHWAYS

DEPARTMENT OF FEEDER ROADS

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES - FIRMS SELECTION)

 

COUNTRY: GHANA

 

NAME OF PROJECT: GHANA MARKET ACCESS AND CONNECTIVITY PROJECT (GMACP)

Project ID No.: P513708

No.

Assignment Titles

Procurement Plan Ref Number

1

Cluster 1A: Consulting Services for Design Review, Construction Supervision and Service Level Maintenance Contract Supervision for Savannah Region in Ghana

GH-DFR-563276-CS-QCBS

 

 

  1. The Government of the Republic of Ghana has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Ghana Market Access and Connectivity Project (GMACP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services for the four (4) separate assignments: Cluster 1A (Consulting Services for Design Review, Construction Supervision and Service Level Maintenance Contract Supervision for Savannah Region in Ghana); Cluster 1B (Consulting Services for Design Review, Construction Supervision and Service Level Maintenance Contract Supervision for Savannah (North Gonja), Upper West and Northern Regions in Ghana); Cluster 2A (Consulting Services for Design Review, Construction Supervision and Service Level Maintenance Contract Supervision for Oti and Volta (Hohoe and Kpando) Regions in Ghana) and Cluster 2B (Consulting Services for Design Review, Construction Supervision and Service Level Maintenance Contract Supervision for Volta and Eastern (Asuogyaman) Regions in Ghana).

This REOI is for the above-mentioned Cluster 1A.

 

The primary objective of this assignment is to ensure that all civil works and maintenance services are executed in full compliance with approved designs, technical specifications, contract conditions, environmental and social safeguards, World Bank Environmental, Health, and Safety (EHS) Guidelines and all other applicable World Bank requirements.

2. The consulting services (“the Services”) include the following among others:

i. Review of detailed designs and related documents for the various lots in cluster 1A.

ii. Supervision of the various groups of road lots in cluster 1A

iii. Monitoring during the defect liability period of the constructed roads.

iv. Supervision of service-level maintenance contracts for the respective constructed roads by the client in cluster 1A.

The implementation period and estimated level of effort (professional person-months) for Key Staff for the assignments is as detailed below:

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained by sending an official request to the email addresses given below.

Main E-mail address: elormnyoagbe@icloud.com

Cc: cynthia.anane@mrh.gov.gh, excelgh@yahoo.com

 

3. Eligibility Requirement for the Assignment

The Ministry of Roads and Highways (MRH), acting through the Department of Feeder Roads, now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

(a) Minimum Mandatory Requirements (pass/fail):

  1. Core business in providing consulting services for road infrastructure projects, including design, supervision, and performance-based maintenance management.
  2. Minimum of ten (10) years of continuous business in providing consulting services for road infrastructure projects, including design, supervision, and maintenance management.
  3. Evidence of experience in at least three (3) road infrastructure consulting assignments of similar scope and complexity (design/design review and construction supervision) completed within the last ten (10) years.
  4. Evidence of experience in at least one (1) road infrastructure consulting assignment of similar scope and complexity (performance-based maintenance management) completed within the last ten (10) years.
  5. Demonstrate prior experience and knowledge in applying FIDIC Conditions of Contract.
  6. Experience in applying good Environmental and Social standards and practices to project management and supervision. Experience and knowledge of the Multilateral Development Banks’ Environmental and Social Framework(s) (ESF), including Environmental, Health, and Safety (EHS) Guidelines, Gender-Based Violence (GBV), Sexual Exploitation and Abuse/Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH) prevention and response requirements.

(b) Desirable qualifications and experience (added advantages):

- Experience working in Sub-Saharan Africa, given the specific geographical, climatic, and social contexts.

- Experience with World Bank-funded or other multilateral/bilateral development bank-funded projects.

 

 Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, the Seventh (7th) Edition, September 2025 (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. The Joint Venture/Sub-consultancy agreement or letter of intent to form a joint venture/a sub-consultancy association signed by every participating member shall be submitted with the Expression of Interest (EOI).

 

4. Submission of Expression of Interest

Interested firms must organize their Expression of Interest in the following order:

Chapter 1

  1. Company Profile
  2. Legal Status (Certificate of Incorporation)
  3. Letter of intent or Agreement to form a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy
  4. Organizational chart, a list of Board of Directors, and beneficial ownership.

Chapter 2

  1. Evidence of experience in at least three (3) road infrastructure consulting assignments of similar scope and complexity (design/design review and construction supervision) completed within the last ten (10) years.
  2. Evidence of experience in at least one (1) road infrastructure consulting assignment of similar scope and complexity (performance-based maintenance management) completed within the last ten (10) years.
  3. A summary of assignments undertaken in Sub-Saharan Africa given the specific geographical, climatic, and social contexts, giving the client’s name and the year in which the assignment was carried out

Chapter 3

  1. Experience in World Bank-funded or other multilateral/bilateral development bank-funded projects.
  2. Experience in applying good Environmental and Social standards and practices to project management and supervision, and in assignments involving Multilateral Development Banks’  Environmental and Social Framework(s) (ESF), including Environmental, Health, and Safety (EHS) Guidelines, Gender-Based Violence (GBV), Sexual Exploitation and Abuse/Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH) prevention and response requirements.

The document must be properly paged, and a table of contents provided.

Consultants will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 0900 to 1700 hours GMT.

Expressions of interest dossiers should be clearly marked “Cluster 1A: Consulting Services for Design Review, Construction Supervision and Service Level Maintenance Contract Supervision for Savannah Region in Ghana” and delivered as an original and three (3) hard copies. In addition, a PDF soft copy must be delivered to the address below (in person or by email) by 16:00 hours GMT on 11th September 2026.
