Exigences techniques spécifiques à ajouter

La portée actuelle du contrôle est principalement centrée sur les travaux de génie civil.

Pour chaque centre de collecte de lait, le cabinet devrait également contrôler :

Installations et équipements

  • les tanks de refroidissement et de stockage ;
  • les groupes frigorifiques et leurs accessoires ;
  • la capacité réelle de refroidissement ;
  • les installations électriques et les protections ;
  • les systèmes solaires, groupes électrogènes ou dispositifs de secours ;
  • les équipements de réception, filtration, pesage et contrôle du lait ;
  • les équipements de laboratoire, lorsqu’ils sont prévus ;
  • les systèmes d’alimentation en eau potable ;
  • les équipements de lavage et de désinfection ;
  • les installations d’évacuation des eaux usées.

Exigences sanitaires et fonctionnelles

  • la séparation entre zones propres et zones sales ;
  • les revêtements lavables et résistants ;
  • la pente et le drainage des sols ;
  • la ventilation ;
  • la protection contre les nuisibles ;
  • la disponibilité de l’eau ;
  • la facilité de nettoyage et de désinfection ;
  • la sécurité sanitaire du lait ;
  • le maintien de la température requise ;
  • la circulation des personnes, véhicules et produits ;
  • la gestion des effluents issus du nettoyage.

Mise en service

Les TDR doivent prévoir :

  • les essais à vide et en charge ;
  • les essais de refroidissement ;
  • la vérification de la stabilité de la température ;
  • la vérification des consommations électriques ;
  • les essais des dispositifs de secours ;
  • la remise des garanties des équipements ;
  • la remise des manuels d’utilisation et d’entretien ;
  • la formation des futurs gestionnaires et opérateurs.

Il faudra également préciser si les équipements sont inclus dans les marchés de travaux ou font l’objet de marchés distincts. Dans ce second cas, le cabinet devra assurer la coordination des interfaces entre bâtiment, électricité, froid et équipements.

THE UNITED REPUBLIC OF TANZANIA

PRIME MINISTER’S OFFICE

REGIONAL ADMINISTRATION AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT

 

MSIMBAZI BASIN DEVELOPMENT PROJECT (MBDP)

IDA CREDIT NO. 7215-TZ

 

TENDER NO. 56/2026/2027/C/13                                                                

FOR

PROVISION OF CONSULTANCY SERVICES TO UNDERTAKE AN ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL IMPACT ASSESSMENT AND RESETTLEMENT ACTION PLAN FOR FLOOD AND EROSION CONTROL INTERVENTIONS IN THE MIDDLE AND UPPER BASIN OF THE MSIMBAZI RIVER IN DAR ES SALAAM

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

1. This request for expressions of interest follows the General Procurement Notice for the Msimbazi Basin Development Project (MBDP) that appeared in the United Nations Development Business (UNDB) online Notice No. OP00221060 of March 29, 2023.

2. The Government of the United Republic of Tanzania has received financing from the International Development Association (IDA) toward the cost of the Msimbazi Basin Development Project (IDA Credit No. 7215-TZ). The Project Development Objective is to strengthen flood resilience and integrated urban development in an economically important and flood-prone area of the Msimbazi River Basin. It is intended that part of the proceeds of the credit will be applied to eligible payments under the contract for Consultancy Services to Undertake an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment, and Resettlement Action Plan for Flood and Erosion Control Interventions in the Middle and Upper Basin of the Msimbazi River in Dar es Salaam.

3. The overall objective of the consulting services is to prepare a comprehensive Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA), Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP), and Resettlement Action Plan (RAP) for the proposed flood and erosion control interventions in the middle and upper basin of the Msimbazi River. The ESIA shall identify environmental and social risks and impacts, assess feasible alternatives, define mitigation and management measures, and support project approval, design integration, procurement, construction, operation, and maintenance. The RAP shall identify all project-affected persons, affected assets, land requirements, livelihood impacts, access restrictions, eligibility criteria, compensation and assistance measures, livelihood restoration measures, institutional arrangements, implementation schedule, grievance procedures, monitoring requirements, and budget necessary to manage resettlement impacts in accordance with Tanzanian law and World Bank ESS5.

4. The specific objectives are to: (i) Establish the environmental and social baseline conditions within the project area of influence, including physical, biological, socioeconomic, health and safety, land-use, livelihood, infrastructure, utility, and cultural heritage aspects; (ii) Identify, predict, and assess potential positive and adverse impacts during pre-construction, construction, operation, maintenance, and decommissioning phases, including direct, indirect, cumulative, induced, and residual impacts; (iii) Assess feasible alternatives, including the no-project option, alternative locations, intervention types, design approaches, construction methods, sequencing options, sediment-management approaches, and nature-based or hybrid solutions; (iv) Recommend practical measures to avoid, minimize, mitigate, manage, compensate for, or offset adverse environmental and social impacts, while enhancing positive outcomes and climate-resilience benefits; (v) Prepare a detailed Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP), including mitigation measures, monitoring requirements, institutional responsibilities, implementation schedule, capacity-building needs, reporting arrangements, grievance-management linkages, and cost estimates; (vi) Prepare environmental and social requirements to be incorporated into feasibility studies, detailed engineering designs, Bills of Quantities, technical specifications, construction methodology, operation and maintenance plans, and bidding documents; (vii) Support PMO-RALG in meeting applicable Tanzanian environmental approval requirements and World Bank environmental and social due diligence requirements; (viii) Prepare a Resettlement Action Plan for all confirmed land acquisition, physical displacement, economic displacement, livelihood impacts, access restrictions, temporary occupation, asset loss, or vulnerability impacts associated with the proposed interventions, temporary works, access routes, associated facilities, and implementation arrangements; (ix) Undertake a census, asset inventory, socio-economic survey, valuation support, and vulnerability assessment of all project-affected persons and affected assets within the confirmed project area of impact; (x) Establish and disclose the cut-off date in coordination with the Client, local authorities, and affected communities, and prepare a verified PAP register and entitlement matrix; (xi) Prepare practical compensation, resettlement assistance, livelihood restoration, transitional support, and vulnerability support measures consistent with Tanzanian requirements, World Bank ESS5, and the project’s relevant environmental and social instruments; and (xii) Ensure that RAP findings are integrated into engineering design, construction sequencing, site handover, bidding documents, implementation arrangements, grievance management, and monitoring.

5. The assignment scope shall cover the selected flood and erosion control intervention areas in the middle and upper basin of the Msimbazi River, including the main Msimbazi River and relevant tributaries such as the Kibangu/Ubungo and Luhanga systems, as well as any other river reaches identified through the engineering screening, feasibility, and design process. The ESIA area of influence shall include, as applicable: (a) the direct footprints of proposed interventions; (b) affected river corridors, floodplains, wetlands, riparian zones, and adjacent land uses; (c) upstream and downstream reaches that may be affected by changes in flow, flooding, erosion, sediment transport, drainage, or river morphology; (d) temporary and associated facilities, including access roads, haul routes, borrow areas, disposal sites, stockpile areas, workers’ facilities, construction camps, staging areas, and temporary works areas; (e) settlements, businesses, farms, public facilities, community assets, utilities, roads, bridges, culverts, and drainage infrastructure that may be affected during construction or operation; and (f) areas that may experience cumulative impacts from multiple interventions within the basin and from other ongoing or planned activities under the wider Msimbazi Basin Development Project.

6. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) can be found at the following website: https://www.tamisemi.go.tz. Requests for clarification should be sent through the following e-mail addresses: cities.project@yahoo.com or cities.project@tamisemi.go.tz, and the Client will send responses to clarifications through the same e-mail addresses.

7. The Permanent Secretary, PMO-RALG, now invites eligible consulting firms to indicate their interest in providing the above services. Interested consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The short-listing criteria are: (a) Type of core business and at least 10 years in relevant business; (b) Relevant similar experience, which should specifically include the following: (i) Experience in similar assignments - information to be provided should include the name of the assignments, the names and full contact addresses of the clients, the contract value (in equivalent US dollars), the period (month/year) of execution of the assignments, and the role played in the assignments (Lead or JV Partner); (ii) Demonstration of experience working in similar conditions; and (c) The firm's technical and managerial capability (provide only the organizational structure, and the general qualifications, field of expertise and number of key personnel). Do not provide the CVs of the staff. Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but they should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a Joint Venture (JV) and/or a Sub-Consultant. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. Therefore, each member of the JV shall independently meet the requirements of the evaluation criteria. The experience, technical & managerial capability of the sub-consultant shall not be evaluated to enhance the qualification of the Lead Firm or JV. Consultants shall not use the Affiliate Member's Managerial, Technical or Experience Capabilities to enhance their qualifications.

Note that: The Request for Expression of Interest (REOI) for this Consultancy Services to Undertake an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment, and Resettlement Action Plan for Flood and Erosion Control Interventions in the Middle and Upper Basin of the Msimbazi River in Dar es Salaam is being advertised at the same time together with another similar Tender for Consultancy Services for Preparation of a Combined Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) and Resettlement Action Plan (RAP) for Area Based Investments in DLAs and Priority Drainage Interventions in Dar es Salaam under DMDP 2; and the assignments in these two Tenders will be executed simultaneously. Hence, in order for a firm shortlisted in the two tenders to be contracted for Consultancy Services in two tenders; it must propose separate Key Experts for each Tender in both Technical and Financial Proposals.

8. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” Sixth Edition, February 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

9. A consulting firm will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

10. Expressions of Interest marked: “EXPRESSION OF INTEREST FOR THE PROVISION OF CONSULTANCY SERVICES TO UNDERTAKE AN ENVIRONMENTAL AND SOCIAL IMPACT ASSESSMENT AND RESETTLEMENT ACTION PLAN FOR FLOOD AND EROSION CONTROL INTERVENTIONS IN THE MIDDLE AND UPPER BASIN OF THE MSIMBAZI RIVER IN DAR ES SALAAM”; should be delivered in written form to the Secretary, Ministerial Tender Board, Prime Minister’s Office, Regional Administration and Local Government (PMO-RALG), CDA Road, Sokoine House, Wing A, Second Floor, Office of the Procurement Management Unit (PMU), Room No. 133, P.O. Assignment Title: Selection of a Consulting Firm for the Design, Development, and Deployment of a Digital Data Protection Compliance Management System for the Data Protection Commission of Zambia

Reference No.: ZM-SZ-554941-CS-QCBS

Background

The Government of the Republic of Zambia (GRZ) has received financing from the World Bank to accelerate countrywide digital transformation through the Digital Zambia Acceleration Project (DZAP) and intends to use part of the proceeds of the credit to accelerate country-wide digital transformation under the Digital Zambia Acceleration Project (DZAP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consulting Services for the Design, Development, and Deployment of a Digital Data Protection Compliance Management System for the Data Protection Commission of Zambia

Objectives of the assignment

The overall objective of this assignment is to deliver a fully functional, secure, and scalable digital DPCMS that serves as the digital backbone of the DPC's regulatory operations, a single, integrated platform through which data handlers register and manage their compliance obligations; data subjects exercise their statutory rights under the Act; the DPC conducts investigations, issues determinations, and enforces the law; and the public accesses transparent regulatory information through open registers and published decisions.

 

The Scope of services

The Consultant shall design, develop, test, deploy, and support a digital DPCMS comprising integrated functional modules. The system shall be responsive across desktop, tablet, and mobile devices; accessible in conformity with WCAG 2.1 Level AA; built in compliance with ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 27701, and OWASP Top 10 security standards; and integrated with the Government Service Bus through ZamConnect and ZamPay as the mandatory primary channel for all DPC revenue collection.

Invitation to eligible Consulting Firms

The SZI hereby invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants shall submit Expressions of Interest (EOIs), including documentation and information demonstrating that they possess the requisite qualifications, relevant experience, and capability to undertake and successfully deliver the Services.

Firms Qualifications

The firm shall meet the following minimum qualifications:

Core business of the firm(s) and years in business.

  • Legal registration as a firm or consortium in Zambia or a country with recognised bilateral trade relations with Zambia.
  • Valid Tax Compliance Certificate (Zambian firms) or equivalent

Relevant experience which should specifically include the following:

  • Minimum five (5) years of operation as an ICT or software development enterprise, with at least three (3) completed government or regulatory compliance management system projects within the last seven (7) years fully delivered, not ongoing with client references and completion certificates.
  • Demonstrated technical capacity in full-stack web application development; cloud or on-premises hosting architecture; RESTful API design and integration; mobile application development for Android and iOS; AI/ML integration for chatbot and predictive analytics; and cybersecurity in conformity with ISO/IEC 27001 and OWASP standards.
  • Experience integrating with government digital ecosystems, payment gateways, or national identity infrastructure; prior experience with Zambia's Government Service Bus, ZamPay, or ZamConnect is an advantage.

 

Technical and Managerial capability of the firm(s) (Provide only the structure of the organization and CVs of the Directors or Principals of the firm. Do not provide CVs of the Experts). Key Experts will not be evaluated at the short-listing stage.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, 3.17 and 3.20 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers – 7th Edition” dated September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest and eligibility.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

The consulting firm will be selected using the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method through an Open International Market Approach, in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Project Financing, 7th Edition (September 2025).

SDTF No. TF C7573-KG: The Ministry of Health of the Kyrgyz Republic's “Primary Health Care Quality Improvement Operation (PHCQIO) Additional Financing” project, financed by the World Bank, announces a competition for the following vacant position:

Date of publication:    11-08-2026

Deadline for applications:    25-08-2026

 

As part of the implementation of the Primary Health Care Quality Improvement Operation (PHCQIO) Additional Financing Project, financed by the World Bank, the Ministry of Health of the Kyrgyz Republic announces a competition for the following vacant position:

 

Technical Consultant with a medical background to support the Ministry of Health in implementing a preferential drug provision scheme under the State Guaranteed Benefits Program

Qualification Requirements:

  • Higher medical education (at least 5 years of experience and skills in the health system, and at least 5 years in the mandatory insurance system);
  • Experience in developing and implementing mechanisms for drug provision within the framework of state health programs, including the formation of drug formularies, the development of mechanisms for selecting health technologies, pricing, drug reimbursement, the organization of drug dispensing, and the monitoring of drug distribution;
  • Experience in analyzing the need for medicines in the health sector, assessing budgetary impacts, and preparing analytical reports on issues related to the financing of drug provision;
  • Experience and skills in drafting regulatory documents and national programs in the fields of health and health insurance, as well as preferential drug provision; experience in conducting  procedures for coordinating draft documents with government agencies, health care organizations, and international organizations and development partners during the implementation of health projects;
  • Experience in conducting expert assessments of medicines for inclusion on lists of preferential medicines;
  • Practical experience in developing, implementing, or improving the State Guaranteed Benefits Program, the Additional Drug Program of Mandatory Health Insurance, and other state programs for financing medical care and drug provision shall be an advantage;
  • Experience in participating in the development or implementation of digital solutions and information systems in healthcare, including the integration of reference databases, registries, classifiers, and other digital components into government information systems. Experience working with the “EDBDMD” information systems, the MHIF's “Electronic Subsidized Prescription,” “Electronic Outpatient Record,” “Electronic Inpatient Record,” and experience working with the “Dary – Darmek” mobile app, as well as participation in projects related to their integration, shall be an advantage;
  • Skills in preparing analytical reports, guidance materials, and presentations; conducting consultations; and working as part of interagency working groups;
  • Ability to collaborate and be solution-oriented, initiative, flexibility, problem-solving skills, and strong communication skills;
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint). Knowledge of Russian and Kyrgyz sufficient to work with recommendations and technical documentation shall be an advantage.

Interested candidates are invited to send their CV, indicating their contact telephone number and position in English and Russian, letters of recommendation from their place of work, copies of relevant diplomas and certificates, as well as the contact details of at least two referees for verification of references, by 18:00 on August 25, 2026, by email: puimzkr@gmail.com; saltanat1281@mail.ru; a_turgunalieva@mz.med.kg; or by mail to Kyrgyzstan, Bishkek, Togolok-Moldo 1a St, 1nd floor, No. 12. Documents must be submitted in PDF format, and resumes must be signed.

Applications without the job title, containing an incomplete set of documents, or received after the deadline will not be considered.

 Only the most suitable candidates will be invited for an interview.

Detailed information regarding the eligibility requirements and technical specifications is available on the EGZ portal in the Announcements section, under Procurements Announced by Projects.

SOLICITAÇÃO DE MANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE ESPECIALISTA EM GESTÃO DE RISCOS SOCIAIS CONSULTORIA INDIVIDUAL HEPRR/C-004

País: Angola

Nome do Projecto: Projecto de Preparação, Resposta e Resiliência a Emergências de Saúde em Angola (HEPRR) Título de Contracto: Contratação de Serviços de Consultoria

Empréstimo No: 9562-AO 

Referência No.: HEPRR-AO/C-004

O Governo de Angola recebeu uma doação no valor equivalente de USD 1.9 milhões de Dólares Norte Americanos, com o Banco Internacional de Reconstrução e Desenvolvimento (BIRD) do Grupo Banco Mundial, para a implementação do Projecto de Preparação, Resposta e Resiliência a Emergências de Saúde em Angola (HEPRR) e pretende aplicar parte dos recursos na contratação de um/uma Especialista em gestão de riscos Sociais.

O objectivo geral desta consultoria é o de acompanhar e analisar os indicadores de impacto social, bem como propor medidas para a mitigação de riscos e impactos sociais relacionados com os Projecto. A consultoria terá a duração de Cinco (5) meses, renováveis em função do desempenho satisfatório, da disponibilidade financeira e das necessidades do projecto. Os termos de referência podem ser obtidos no endereço electrónico abaixo indicado.

O Projecto de Preparação, Resposta e Resiliência a Emergências de Saúde em Angola (HEPRR), convida por este meio os consultores individuais ("Consultores") elegíveis a manifestarem o seu interesse em prestar os Serviços. Os consultores interessados deverão fornecer informações que demonstrem que possuem as qualificações requeridas e experiência relevante para executar os serviços, submetendo o seu curriculum vitae, certificados/diplomas académicos, comprovativos de experiência profissional e outros documentos de suporte que se achem necessários para a candidatura. 

O(A) Consultor(a) deverá possuir as seguintes qualificações:

Formação Académica

• Possuir formação superior ao nível de licenciatura em Ciências Sociais, nomeadamente Sociologia, Desenvolvimento Social/Comunitário, Direitos Humanos e áreas afins;

• Possuir formação ao nível de pós-graduação, Mestrado ou Especialização em Ciências Sociais ou áreas afins é uma vantagem; Experiência Profissional

• Possuir um curso, experiência ou treinamento em Violência Baseada no Género é uma vantagem;

• Deve possuir oito (8) ou mais anos de experiência na gestão de projectos sociais, preferencialmente, relacionada a actividades sociais em Saúde e desenvolvimento social ou comunitário;

• Experiência com as Políticas de Gestão Ambiental e Sociais do Banco Mundial e noções básicas sobre o Quadro Ambiental e Social; e a legislação nacional angolana e correspondente, é uma vantagem;

• Experiência na condução e monitoria de EIAS/PGAS é uma vantagem;

• Experiência na implementação (concepção, implementação e monitorização de actividades) de mecanismos de gestão de reclamações é uma vantagem;

• Experiência na implementação de planos de mitigação social e em avaliação de Impactos Sociais;

• Experiência na implementação (concepção, implementação e monitorização de actividades) de processos de consulta pública;

• Comprovada capacidade técnica, analítica, escrita e comunicação na redação de relatórios de progresso e comunicação de resultados;

• Domínio da língua portuguesa;

• Fluência na escrita e fala em inglês é uma vantagem.

• Bons conhecimentos de informática na óptica do utilizador;

• Experiência em projectos de inclusão de grupos de desfavorecidos, incluindo comunidades de minorias etnolinguísticas e pessoas portadoras de deficiência constitui uma vantagem;

• Vantagem será dada a candidatos com experiência na gestão de Mecanismos de Reclamações (MR) e no seguimento de incidentes relacionados com Violência Baseada no Género (VBG);

• Conhecimento dos aspectos relativos à higiene e segurança ocupacional e saúde e segurança nas comunidades;

• Conhecimentos em preparação de materiais de comunicação e sensibilização para a mudança de comportamentos são uma vantagem;

• Experiência em trabalhar em projectos de desenvolvimento em países africanos e, em particular, em Angola, será um ponto de vantagem.

Os consultores serão avaliados com base nas Normas e Regulamentos de Aquisições do Banco Mundial para Mutuários de Financiamentos de Projectos de Investimento de Setembro de 2023, pelo que deverão ter em atenção à Secção III, parágrafos 3.14, 3.16, e 3.17 das referidas Normas, que definem a política do Banco Mundial sobre o conflito de interesses. O referido documento pode ser consultado na seguinte hiperligação: https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/6c0602876d68949e80820507d90a14ed 0290012023/original/Procurement-Regulations-September-2023.pdf.

O(A) Consultor(a) será selecionado com base no método de contratação de Consultores Individuais de acordo com as Normas e Regulamentos de Aquisições em vigor (Setembro 2023). Os Consultores interessados poderão obter informação adicional, incluindo os TORs (Termos de Referência) no endereço abaixo indicado de Segunda Feira à Sexta Feira entre as 8H00 – 15H00. As manifestações de interesse (Currículo, cópia dos certificados de habilitações académicas, avaliação de desempenho e outra informação pertinente) deverão ser enviadas até ao dia 18 de Agosto de 2026 às 15H00 (Horário de Angola).

Messieurs, Mesdames,

  1. Le Gouvernement du Burkina Faso a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour financer le coût du Projet d’accélération de la transformation digitale du Burkina Faso (PACTDIGITAL-BF), et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce financement pour effectuer des paiements au titre du Marché « acquisition d’équipements informatiques et de matériels de bureau au profit des parties prenantes du PACTDIGITAL (03 lots) ». 
  2. Pour ce marché, l’Emprunteur utilisera la méthode de décaissement par Paiement Direct, telle que définie dans les Directives de Décaissement de la Banque mondiale pour le Financement de Projet d’Investissement, (FPI). »
  3. La Direction des Marchés Publics du Ministère de la Transition Digitale, des Postes et des Communications Electroniques sollicite des offres fermées de la part de soumissionnaires éligibles et répondant aux qualifications requises pour fournir des équipements informatiques et de matériels de bureau au profit des parties prenantes du Projet d’accélération de la transformation digitale du Burkina Faso et qui seront livrés au siège du projet à Ouagadougou.
  4. L’appel d’offres porte sur l’acquisition d’équipements informatiques et de matériels de bureau au profit des parties prenantes du PACTDIGITAL. Il est composé de trois lots et reparti comme ci-dessous :
  • Lot 1 : Acquisition d’ordinateurs portables spécifiques ;
  • Lot 2 : Acquisition de matériels informatiques et d’équipements divers;
  • Lot 3 : Acquisition de matériels de bureau et informatiques.

Un Soumissionnaire peut présenter une offre pour un ou plusieurs marchés, comme précisé dans le Document d’Appel d’Offres. Un Soumissionnaire désirant offrir un rabais dans le cas où plusieurs marchés lui seraient attribués, sera autorisé à le faire, mais il devra indiquer ces rabais dans le Formulaire d’Offre.

Le délai d’exécution est de quatre-vingt-dix (90) jours pour les lots 1 et 2 et soixante (60) jours pour le lot 3.

  1. La passation du Marché sera conduite par Mise en Concurrence internationale (AOI) telle que définie dans le « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement » de la Banque mondiale, septième édition de septembre 2025 », et ouvert à tous les soumissionnaires de pays éligibles tels que définis dans ledit Règlement.
  2. Les Offres seront évaluées conformément au processus d'évaluation défini dans le dossier d'appel d'offres. KINGDOM OF CAMBODIA

NATION RELIGION KING

Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries

General Directorate of Animal Health and Production (GDAHP)

Cambodia Inclusive Livestock Value Chains Project (CILVCP), Grant No. TF0C7108, P180535

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

Assignment Title     : Consultancy Service for Digital Livestock Extension System (DLES)

Method                    : Quality and Cost-based Selection (QCBS)

Reference No.         : Ref. CILVCP-CS-004

Date Published       : August 10, 2026

The Royal Government of Cambodia (RGC) through the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, General Directorate of Animal Health and Production (GDAHP) has received a Trust Fund from the Global Agriculture and Food Security Program (GAFSP) for a US$20 Million Grant toward the cost of the Cambodia Inclusive Livestock Value Chains Project (CILVCP) for five years starting from 2025 to 2029 and intends to apply part of the proceeds of this Grant to payments under the contract for Consulting Service.

The consulting services (“the Services”): Consultancy Service for Digital Livestock Extension System (DLES).

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the primary procurement stage for the assignment are attached to this request for expressions of interest or can be found via 

https://1drv.ms/b/c/3bcf6b3d288b9af2/IQBMU5EP1qVJTIW0stUgWueXAb_aUJhZedfxNBy8FwEsK28?e=KIMz9D

The General Directorate of Animal Health and Production (GDAHP) now invites eligible consulting firms/ Non-Governmental Organizations “Consultants” to indicate their interest in providing services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

Shortlisting consultants will be required to meet the following minimum criteria:

  1. Core Business and Years in Business: Demonstrate 5-6 years of continuous operational experience in areas relevant to this assignment
  2. Specific Experience: Demonstrate at least 6-7 years of experience in designing, developing, and implementing digital platforms, ICT service delivery systems, and/or multimedia IEC materials, especially for agriculture, livestock, or rural development programs/ 4-5 previous contracts of similar scope and nature to the assignment.
  3. Technical Capability: Demonstrated limited team composition and availability of experts as specified in Terms of Reference (TOR).
  4. Managerial Capability: Demonstrates 4-5 contracts of similar scope implemented in East Asia and the Pacific (EAP). Experience in Cambodia will be an advantage.  

The Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Quality and Cost-based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the World Bank's “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers,” updated in September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”).

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 7:00-11:30 and 14:00-17:30 (local time).

Expressions of Interest must be delivered in electronic and hard copy with a submission letter (1 electronic copy and 2 hard copies) which clearly indicates the assignment title and reference number to the address below, no later than August 25, before 17:00 (Cambodian local time).

REPUBLIC OF TÜRKYE

MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, URBANIZATION AND CLIMATE CHANGE (MoEUCC)

GENERAL DIRECTORATE OF CONSTRUCTION AFFAIRS (GDCA)

PREPARATION IN RELATION TO TÜRKYE UNIVERSITY HOSPITAL RESILIENCE PROJECT (P515155)

CONSULTANCY SERVICES FOR DESIGN REVIEW OF THE 150-BED KAHRAMANMARA SÜTÇÜ MAM UNIVERSITY HOSPITAL

Reference No: (GFPP/CS-DESREV-02)

1. The Ministry of Environment, Urbanization and Climate Change (MoEUCC) has applied financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.  

2. The consulting services (“the Services”) include comprehensive Design Review and validation of the existing technical design packages for the new 150-Bed Kahramanmara Sütçü mam University Hospital. 

3. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://turhap.csb.gov.tr/

4. The General Directorate of Construction Affairs (GDCA) invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.  

 5.  A consulting firm is allowed to submit the expression of interest alone if it considers itself to be fully qualified on its own for the assignment, as it is not mandatory for consultants to associate with any other firm(s), whether foreign or local. Alternatively, if consultants themselves choose to associate to enhance their qualifications and capability for the assignment, then such associations may either be as a Joint Venture (i.e. all members of the joint venture shall be jointly and severally responsible) and/or Sub-consultants (i.e. the Consultant will be responsible, including for the services of the sub-consultant).  In case of an association, the Consultants must explain in the EOI submission (a) the rationale for forming the association and (b) the anticipated role and relevant qualifications of each member of the Joint Venture and/or of each sub-consultant for carrying out the assignment, to justify the proposed inclusion of the JV members and/or sub-consultants in the association. Failure to provide the above explanation in the Expression of Interest may risk the association not being shortlisted for the assignment.  Please note that in the evaluation of EOIs of associations for shortlisting purposes, only the qualifications of the JV members will be taken into account whereas the qualifications of proposed sub-consultants will not be considered. 

6.  The shortlisting/selection criteria are as follows, in which specific experience of the Consultant relevant to the assignment will be considered of paramount importance:   

General experience of the Consultant (as a firm):

  • Established as a firm for at least the last ten (10 years) in the business of providing engineering design services.

Specific Experienceof theConsultant (as afirm)relevant to the assignment:

  1. consulting services contracts completed by the firm during the last 15 years for the comprehensive construction design or design review of hospital buildings of similar size.
  2. consulting services contracts completed by the firm during the last 15 years for the comprehensive construction design or design review of buildings (other than hospitals) of similar size.
  3. consulting services contracts completed by the firm during the last 15 years for the comprehensive construction design or design review of buildings with seismic base isolation.

7.  To demonstrate their qualifications and experience in meeting the above shortlisting/selection criteria, Consultants are requested to submit, at a minimum, the supporting documentation listed below.  A consultant firm can only use its own qualifications and experience and not of its parent, sister or subsidiary companies or its employees.  

i. The firm's incorporation/trade/registration documents issued by the concerned government authority of the country of the firm. 

ii. The firm’s company brochures including the core areas of business; and 

iii. Completed Form-1 (It is kindly requested from the interested firms to provide the information above with an excel sheet given in the https://turhap.csb.gov.tr/) to provide information of similar contracts. This should include the name and reference number of the contract, brief description of the scope of work, contract amount, period of the contract, name of the client and country of assignment, and role of the Consultant in the contract.  Copies of completion certificates/references of Clients of completed contracts are not required to be submitted with the EoI. In the subsequent stage at the time of submission of proposals, the Client may request the shortlisted consultants to submit such supporting completion certificates.

8.  The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to (i) paragraphs 3.16 & 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Project Financing (Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services Procurement Regulation (September 2025), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

 9.  A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

10. Further information can be obtained at the address below from 10.00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. (Türkiye Local Time).

11.  Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by fax, or by e-mail) by August 31, 2026 till 3:00 p.m. (Türkiye Local Time)

SOLICITAÇÃO DE MANIFESTAÇÃO DE INTERESSE 1 ESPECIALISTA JÚNIOR PARA O CENTRO DE OPERAÇÕES DE EMERGÊNCIAS E SAÚDE PÚBLICA

CONSULTORIA INDIVIDUAL HEPRR-AO/C-009

País: Angola

Nome do Projecto: Projecto de Preparação, Resposta e Resiliência a Emergências de Saúde em Angola (HEPRR) Título de Contracto: Contratação de Serviços de Consultoria

Empréstimo No.: 9562-AO RFP Referência No.: HEPRR-AO/C-009

O Governo de Angola recebeu uma doação no valor equivalente de USD 1.9 milhões de Dólares Norte Americanos, com o Banco Internacional de Reconstrução e Desenvolvimento (BIRD) do Grupo Banco Mundial, para a implementação do Projecto de Preparação, Resposta e Resiliência a Emergências de Saúde em Angola (HEPRR) e pretende aplicar parte dos recursos na contratação de um (1) Especialista Júnior para o Centro de Operações de Emergências e Saúde Pública -COESP.

O objectivo geral desta consultoria visa assegurar a prestação de assistência técnica à Direção Nacional de Saúde Pública (DNSP) na coordenação, implementação, expansão e operacionalização do Centro de Operações de Emergências e Saúde Pública - COESP, fortalecendo as capacidades de preparação, vigilância, coordenação e resposta às emergências de saúde pública, em conformidade com o Regulamento Sanitário Internacional (RSI 2005) e os objetivos do Projeto de Preparação, Resposta e Resiliência às Emergências de Saúde (HEPRR).

A consultoria terá a duração de Cinco (5) meses, renováveis em função do desempenho satisfatório, da disponibilidade financeira e das necessidades do projecto. Os termos de referência podem ser obtidos no endereço electrónico abaixo indicado.

O Projecto de Preparação, Resposta e Resiliência a Emergências de Saúde em Angola (HEPRR), convida por este meio os consultores individuais ("Consultores") elegíveis a manifestarem o seu interesse em prestar os Serviços. Os consultores interessados deverão fornecer informações que demonstrem que possuem as qualificações requeridas e experiência relevante para executar os serviços, submetendo o seu curriculum vitae, certificados/diplomas académicos, comprovativos de experiência profissional e outros documentos de suporte que se achem necessários para a candidatura.

O(A) Consultor(a) deverá possuir as seguintes qualificações:

Formação Académica

Licenciatura em Medicina, em Enfermagem, ou áreas afins;

Mestrado ou Especialização em Saúde Pública, Gestão de Operações ou Desenvolvimento Internacional representam vantagens adicionais;

Experiência Profissional

• Mínimo de 5 anos de experiência em resposta a emergências de saúde pública, com experiência nacional ou internacional na implementação e fortalecimento de programas de resposta a emergência, incluindo COESP;

• Conhecimento e experiência de implementação do Regulamento Sanitário Internacional (RSI 2005), diretrizes internacionais de resposta a emergências, e vigilância epidemiológica;

• Conhecimento e experiência de aplicações e ferramentas de Office baseados em ICT’s (processamento de texto, planilhas e processamento de dados, PowerPoint);

• Excelente domínio da Língua Portuguesa e conhecimento da Língua Inglesa.

Os consultores serão avaliados com base nas Normas e Regulamentos de Aquisições do Banco Mundial para Mutuários de Financiamentos de Projectos de Investimento de Setembro de 2023, pelo que deverão ter em atenção à Secção III, parágrafos 3.14, 3.16, e 3.17 das referidas Normas, que definem a política do Banco Mundial sobre o conflito de interesses. O referido documento pode ser consultado na seguinte hiperligação: https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/6c0602876d68949e80820507d90a14ed 0290012023/original/Procurement-Regulations-September-2023.pdf. O(A) Consultor(a) será selecionado com base no método de contratação de Consultores Individuais de acordo com as Normas e Regulamentos de Aquisições em vigor (Setembro 2023).

Os Consultores interessados poderão obter informação adicional, incluindo os TORs (Termos de Referência) no endereço abaixo indicado de Segunda Feira à Sexta Feira entre as 8H00 – 15H00. As manifestações de interesse (Currículo, cópia dos certificados de habilitações académicas, avaliação de desempenho e outra informação pertinente) deverão ser enviadas até ao dia 18 de Agosto de 2026 às 15H00 (Horário de Angola).

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(LEARN-IC-NIO-2.8.1 – Content Expert 3 (Mathematics))


 

UKRAINE

Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program

Grant No. TF0C5794

 

Assignment Title: Content Expert 3 (Mathematics)

Reference No. LEARN-IC-NIO-2.8.1

Ukraine and World bank have signed the agreements for the Program “Lifting Education Access and Resilience in times of Need in Ukraine Program” (hereinafter referred to as the LEARN or Operation). 

LEARN was developed to address critical challenges and provide essential support to the education sector, aligning with the Ministry of Education and Science’s (MoES) Strategic Action Plan. The objectives of the Operation are to (i) improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) strengthen management capacity of the education system.

The objective of the Consultant's assignment is to develop high-quality educational materials in the field of mathematics, aligned with NUS standards. The Content Expert will ensure the materials are mathematically accurate, pedagogically effective, and cater to the diverse needs of students and educators.

The Consultant will be contracted through competitive selection in line with the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”). 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the Procurement Regulations, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

MOES now invites qualified interested persons to submit their expression of interest in Ukrainian and English as provided in the Terms of reference.  

The detailed Terms of Reference and submission modalities for the assignment are attached to this Request for Expression of Interest.

The deadline for submission of applications is 14:00 am Kyiv time August 19, 2026.  

TERMS OF REFERENCE

 

for Consulting Services (Individual Consultant)

Content Expert 3 (Mathematics)

Contract No. LEARN-IC-NIO-2.8.1

Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program

URTF Grant No. TF0C5794

 

 

  1.  BACKGROUND

 

Ukraine and the World Bank have signed the agreements for the Program "Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program" (hereinafter referred to as the LEARN). The objectives of the LEARN are: to (i) improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) to strengthen the management capacity of the education system.

 

The total financing for the Operation is US$451 million using a combination of the World Bank's financial instruments: Program-for-Results (PforR) complemented by Investment Project Financing (IPF).

The Program-for-Results (PforR) is funded by a US$235 million credit provided by Bank resources, supported by credit enhancement from the Advancing Needed Credit Enhancement for Ukraine (ADVANCE Ukraine) Trust Fund, which is backed by the Government of Japan. This is formalized under the Financing Agreement between Ukraine and the International Development Association for the Program (CREDIT NUMBER 7626-UA). An additional US$150 million is provided under the Special Program for Ukraine and Moldova Recovery (SPUR) of the International Development Association (IDA) Crisis Facility, as outlined in the Loan Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development for the Program (LOAN NUMBER 9721-UA). Financing Agreement (Additional Financing: Lifting Education Access and Resilience in Times of Need in Ukraine Program) between Ukraine and the International Development Association (CREDIT NUMBER 7905-UA) was signed in the amount of US$4.9 million.

Furthermore, US$30 million in Investment Project Financing (IPF) is secured under the Grant Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association, acting as the administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction, and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (URTF GRANT NUMBER TF0C5794).

Furthermore, US$31.1 million in Additional Financing is provided through grant resources, consisting of US$30.0 million from the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction, and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund and US$1.1 million from the Global Partnership for Education Fund. This additional financing is formalized under the Grant Agreement between Ukraine and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the International Development Association, jointly acting as a Supervising Entity for the Global Partnership for Education Fund and as administrator of the Ukraine Relief, Recovery, Reconstruction, and Reform Multi-Donor Trust Fund (URTF GRANT NUMBER TF0D0612; GPE GRANT NUMBER TF0D0613), and supports activities related to the continued implementation of the Program.

 

LEARN was developed to address critical challenges and provide essential support to the education sector, aligning with the Ministry of Education and Science’s (MoES) Strategic Action Plan.

LEARN will focus on supporting the Strategic Action Plan Priority 2: School education and the New Ukrainian School (NUS). The continuation of the NUS reform is a key priority of the MoES.

The objectives of the Program are to (i) improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) strengthen management capacity of the education system.

The Program is implemented in Ukraine by the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine (MoES) with the support of the World Bank Group. The implementation period is 2024-2027.

More detailed information is given at the link https://projects.worldbank.org/en/projects-operations/project-detail/P504171

 

The Operation will focus on supporting the Strategic Action Plan Priority 2: School education and the New Ukrainian School (NUS). The continuation of the NUS reform is a key priority of the MoES.

 

The objectives of the Operation are to (i) improve teaching and learning conditions; and (ii) strengthen management capacity of the education system.

 

For this program, "teaching and learning conditions" refer to three critical factors of education service delivery:

 

i. safety, including shelters as a pre-condition for schools to open for in-person learning and free and inclusive school bus transportation for students living further distances from schools;

 

ii. learning materials, especially updated textbooks and age-appropriate learning materials in line with the NUS model; and

 

iii. teachers trained on NUS standards, principles, and the use of the updated learning materials.

 

Meanwhile, "management capacity of the education system" refers to institutional capabilities to plan, allocate, and monitor resources based on robust data at the student and school levels.

 

The NUS Implementation Office (NIO) will be established by the Ministry as an advisory and consultative body. The NIO's primary purpose is to support and implement the New Ukrainian School (NUS) reform by providing expert guidance, strategic oversight, and coordination of reform initiatives across Ukraine.

 

  1.  OBJECTIVE

The objective of this assignment is to develop high-quality educational materials in the field of mathematics, aligned with NUS standards. The Content Expert will ensure the materials are mathematically accurate, pedagogically effective, and cater to the diverse needs of students and educators.

  1. SCOPE OF SERVICES

 

The Consultant shall provide the following services, including but not limited to:

 

  • Develop and adapt educational materials in the field of mathematics in alignment with NUS standards.
  • Ensure the mathematical accuracy and pedagogical soundness of all developed content.
  • Review and enhance existing educational resources, making recommendations for improvements.
  • Collaborate with other content experts and the Content Experts Coordinator to ensure consistency across educational materials.
  • Provide expertise in creating content that fosters problem-solving and critical thinking skills in students.

 

  1. REPORTING

 

The Content Expert reports directly to the Content Experts Coordinator. Monthly reports detailing progress, challenges, and completed tasks must be submitted, along with time sheets.

  1. PROVIDED RESOURCES

 

MoES shall provide the Consultant with the information necessary to carry out his/her assignment in a timely manner. MoES shall provide the Consultant with a workplace, including necessary equipment to carry out his/her functions (e.g. PC, communications and office equipment).

 

  1. QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS

Minimum Requirements:

  • At least 3 years of professional experience in developing or reviewing educational materials in mathematics.
  • Knowledge of NUS standards and principles.
  • Experience in the education sector, preferably in school-level mathematics education.
  • Advanced proficiency in Ukrainian.

Desired Skills and Qualifications:

  • Strong understanding of mathematical concepts and pedagogy.
  • Ability to develop engaging, inclusive, and age-appropriate educational materials.
  • Attention to detail and ability to meet deadlines.
  • Effective communication and teamwork skills.

 

  1. PERIOD AND LOCATION OF EMPLOYMENT

 

The Consultant shall provide his/her services until August 31, 2027. The contract may be extended subject to satisfactory performance and mutual agreement between the Consultant and the Ministry of Education and Science (MoES) during the Project financing period.

 

The Consultant shall provide his/her services on a full-time basis.

 

The incumbent will be based in Kyiv, Ukraine. The Consultant should be required and expected to take business trips to other regions of Ukraine to support implementation of the Project.

 

VIII. APPLICATION PACKAGE

 

Interested persons should submit their CVs in Ukrainian and English at the following email address: kateryna.kovtun@mon.gov.ua, Cc: serhiy.artemenko@uiherp.org and maryna.chubenko@mon.gov.ua  indicating the email subject: " LEARN-IC-NIO-2.8.1: Selection of Content Expert 3 (Mathematics): [NAME]".

 

The deadline for submission of the documents is 14:00 am Kyiv time August 19, 2026.

 

If the Consultant fails to provide CVs in both languages, the Client reserves the right to reject the Consultant's application.

CENTRAL PROJECTS COORDINATION UNIT (CPCU)
Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs

                                         The Gambia Infrastructure Project (GIP)

                   Request for Expressions of Interest for Consulting Service

Country: The Republic of the Gambia

Project Title: The Gambia Infrastructure Project (GIP)

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for the Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) for NRA’s 150km of Rural and Urban Roads under the Gambia Infrastructure Project

Procurement Method: Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS)   

Reference No.   GM-CPCU - MOFEA-527994-CS-CQS

Background:

The government of the Republic of the Gambia, under the World Bank (WB) Infrastructure Project has received an IDA Grant in an indicative amount equivalent to US$52.56 million available through The Gambia’s national IDA. The bank intends to apply a portion of this grant to eligible payments under a consultancy contract for the provision of Consultancy Services for the Development of Electricity Anti-Theft and Infrastructure Protection Regulation.

The consulting services include Consultancy Services for the Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) for NRA’s 150km of Rural and Urban Roads  under the Gambia Infrastructure Project

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be collected from the address bellowed.

Ms. Ndey Anta Taal Project coordinator, Central Project Coordination Unit, Royal Insurance Building, OIC highway, Kotu Tel:7555502/3971756. Email:/msanyang@cpcumof.gm /gip.procurement@cpcumof.gm / rsey@cpcumof.gm/mbt.senghore@cpcumof.gm  

The Central Project Coordination Unit – Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.:

 

Key Experts and Required Qualifications

The team should be composed of the profiles:

No.

Key Expert

Minimum Qualification & Experience

1

Team Leader- Senior Environmental and Social specialist

  • Must hold a master’s degree or equivalent in Environmental Science or Environmental Engineering
  • at least 8-10 years of working experience in environmental activities particularly in Environment and Social Impacts on Infrastructure projects.
  • Proven experience in preparing World Bank Safeguards documents and knowledge in World Bank environmental and social framework (ESF) will be appreciated.
  •  Proven experience planning and conducting field missions and stakeholder engagement; strong team leadership and project management skills.
  • Locally based and proven knowledge and experience of the local regulations, institutional arrangements, context of working experience in Environment and Social issues to ESIA and ESMP preparations.
  • Excellent English; working knowledge of at least one local language is an advantage.
  • Overall technical leadership and quality assurance of ESIA/ESMP, alignment with national law and WB ESF.
  • Integration of crosscutting themes (gender, SEA/SH, climate, biodiversity, inclusion of vulnerable groups).
  • ESIA implementation plan and roles/responsibilities matrix; inputs to procurement (ESHS clauses, CoC, KPIs); presentation to stakeholders/regulator.

2

Environmental specialist

Qualification and Skills

  • Must hold a master’s degree or equivalent in Environmental Science/Environmental Engineering or equivalent
  • Proficiency in environmental analysis tools: GIS/remote sensing, sampling design, data management, and application of WBG EHS Guidelines.
  • Excellent written, presentation and reporting skills
  • Fluent in English with excellent written and spoken skills
  • Working knowledge of one or more local languages will be an advantage
  • 5–10 years of experience leading environmental components of ESIAs/ESMPs for infrastructure (Transport sector preferred), ideally with experience in The Gambia.  
  • Demonstrated capacity in baseline development (air/noise, water, soil, biodiversity/ecosystem services), impact/risk assessment, and design of avoidance/minimization/mitigation measures. Prior experience in preparing ESIAs or ESMPs involving subproject screening checklist and monitoring.
  • Fieldwork leadership: planning and overseeing surveys, supervising environmental monitoring, and ensuring seasonal considerations are captured.  
  • Crosscutting capabilities: emergency preparedness and response, energy safety, pollution prevention (air/noise/water), waste and hazardous materials management (including e-waste).

3

Social and Gender Specialist

  • Must hold a master’s degree or equivalent in the Social Sciences (i.e., sociology, political science), Human Science or equivalent
  • Strong IT and data skills (qualitative/quantitative methods, data management), and excellent communication (writing, presentations, reporting).
  • Proficient in undertaking inclusive and participatory community and stakeholder consultation, especially with vulnerable populations
  • Fluent in English with excellent written and spoken skills. Working knowledge in one or more local languages will be an advantage
  • Excellent written, presentation and reporting skills
  • At least 8 years of working experience in social activities, including assessment of social risk and impact, particularly in public consultation on infrastructure projects, especially with vulnerable or traditionally marginalized groups.
  • Experience with conducting inclusive and participatory stakeholder consultations, gender disaggregated collection, understanding of including vulnerable groups in social assessments is an asset.
  • Experience working on gender and/or GBV prevention and response programming as well as with the guiding principles for the ethical collection, management, and sharing of data related to GBV is required.  
  • Experience establishing and operating project grievance mechanisms (community and worker GRMs), and in designing culturally appropriate engagement strategies.  
  • Familiarity with the World Bank ESF and national social regulations and practices.
  • Working proficiency in at least one local language (e.g., Fula, Mandinka, Wolof) is required.

4

Occupational Health and Safety Specialist

  • Master’s degree (or equivalent) in occupational health and safety, industrial hygiene, public health, environmental engineering, civil engineering, or occupational medicine.
  • 5–10 years of proven experience managing OHS risks and OSHA/WBG EHS requirements on infrastructure projects (e.g., roads, construction), including site supervision and contractor management.
  • Demonstrated expertise in hazard identification and risk assessment (HIRA), job safety analysis (JSA), emergency preparedness and response, incident/accident investigation, and root cause analysis.
  • Practical experience developing and implementing OHS plans safe work procedures, PPE programs, and training/toolbox talks.
  • Ability to develop the OHS sections of the ESMP (policies, procedures, and performance standards) and define implementation requirements to be reflected in bidding documents and contracts (ESHS clauses and Codes of Conduct).
  • Familiarity with national OHS legislation and international good practice (OSHA/ILO/IFC), including high-risk topics: traffic and road safety in work zones, electrical safety, work at height, lifting operations, confined spaces, heavy equipment.
  • Experience drafting incident/accident notification protocols and investigation frameworks (aligned with 24/48hour reporting), and proposing leading/lagging indicators and monitoring arrangements for inclusion in the ESMP.
  • Capacity to prepare training outlines and toolbox talk guidance to be included in the ESMP for later use by contractors/supervision teams.
  • Strong analytical and technical writing skills to produce clear ESIA/ESMP text and templates; ability to work independently and collaborate within a multidisciplinary ESIA team.

5

Mapping/GIS/Traffic specialist 

  • BSc. GIS/Remote Sensing or other related courses 
  • At least 5 years’ post-graduation experience. 
  • At least three (3) years’ Specific experience in similar assignment. 
  • Participation in similar role in at least two multi-lateral funded projects in the last 6 years including World Bank. 
  • Evidence of familiarity with GIS, Arc Info, ArcMap GIS Pro and other Geo Spatial Design Software 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” (September 2023 revised February 2025 seventh edition September 2025) (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS) set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Invitation for Bids

Date: July 20, 2026

Bid No.: 0733-26093275

1.The Government of the People’s Republic of China has received a loan from the World Bank to finance the China: Emerging Infectious Diseases Prevention, Preparedness and Response Project – Hainan Province Project (Global “One Health” Hainan Demonstration Project), and intends to apply part of the proceeds of this loan to make eligible payments under the contract for the Procurement of Equipment for Provincial CDC, Municipal/County CDCs and Sentinel Sites (Contract No.: HN-G-55).

2.CITIC International Tendering Co., Ltd. (the Procurement Agent), entrusted by Hainan Provincial Disease Control Bureau (the Purchaser), now invites eligible and qualified bidders to submit sealed bids for the following goods and related services:

Contract No.

HN-G-55

Contract Title

Procurement of Equipment for the Provincial CDC, Municipal/County CDCs, and Sentinel Surveillance Sites

Main Types and Quantities of Goods

Light incubators, CO incubators, biosafety tissue grinders, spectrophotometers, single-person clean benches, automatic nucleic acid extractors, stereomicroscopes, -80°C ultra-low temperature freezers, biological specimen cabinets, and other equipment, as well as related services. The detailed requirements are specified in Chapter VI “Schedule of Requirements” of the Bidding Document.

Delivery Period

60 calendar days from the date of contract signing.

3.This procurement will be conducted through National Competitive Procurement (NCP) using the Request for Bids method specified in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (the “Procurement Regulations”). All eligible bidders meeting the requirements of the Procurement Regulations are eligible to bid.

4.Interested eligible bidders may obtain further information from the address specified in this Invitation for Bids and may inspect or purchase the Bidding Documents from July 20, 2026, until the bid submission deadline of August 20, 2026, during the following hours each day (excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and statutory holidays): 9:00–11:30 and 13:30–17:00 (Beijing Time).

5.Prospective bidders should note the provisions on eligibility and conflict of interest set forth in Clause 4 of the Instructions to Bidders of the Bidding Documents. Any bidder having a conflict of interest shall be deemed ineligible.

6.The qualification requirements for bidders include:

Business Scale

The bidder’s average annual turnover for the most recent three years (2023–2025) shall be no less than RMB 37 million.

Contract Experience

The bidder shall have successfully completed, as a supplier, at least one contract for the supply of laboratory instruments or equipment of a similar nature and complexity to the products to be procured under this project during the past three years (from January 1, 2023 to the present). The scope of such supply contract shall include a stereomicroscope, and the value of the single contract shall be no less than RMB 4 million.

The bidder shall provide supporting documents meeting the above requirements, which shall at least include the contract agreement, acceptance certificate issued by the user, and payment receipt/proof of contract payment, etc. The contract copies included in the bid documents shall at least contain the following pages of the contract demonstrating relevant information: the cover page of the contract showing the project name, procurement contents, contract signing date, and contract amount, as well as the page bearing signatures and official seals of the contracting parties. The bidder shall also provide the name and contact information of the end user’s contact person.

Technical Experience

The stereomicroscope to be supplied shall have a minimum production history of one (1) year, and at least one (1) unit/set of such product shall have been sold and completed its warranty period. The bidder shall provide supporting documents demonstrating compliance with the above requirements, including copies of documents such as sales contracts for similar goods.

Production Capacity

Not Applicable.

Financial Position

The bidder’s audited annual financial statements (including the balance sheet and income statement) for the most recent three years (2023, 2024, and 2025) shall demonstrate the bidder’s sound financial position and long-term profitability. The minimum requirement is that the bidder’s net assets (calculated as total assets minus total liabilities) for each of the three years shall be positive.

Cash Flow Capacity

The bidder shall have sufficient available liquid assets, credit facilities, and other financing resources to meet the cash flow requirements for contract performance, taking into account the bidder’s other ongoing contracts. The minimum required amount shall be no less than RMB 1.5 million.

Litigation History

The total amount of pending claims, arbitration proceedings, or other litigation shall not exceed 50% of the bidder’s net assets.

The joint venture bidding is acceptable for this procurement. The maximum number of members in a joint venture shall be two (2), and either the lead partner or the other joint venture member shall meet the above-mentioned qualification requirements.

Further details are provided in the Bidding Documents.

7. Interested eligible bidders may submit an application for purchasing the Bidding Documents to the address specified in this Invitation for Bids and shall pay a non-refundable fee of RMB 1,000. Payment may be made in cash or by direct bank transfer to the account of the Procurement Agent (Account Name: CITIC International Tendering Co., Ltd.; Bank Name: China CITIC Bank Beijing Sanyuanqiao Branch; Account No.: 8110701013102383606). The Bidding Documents will be delivered by mail. The Purchaser and the Procurement Agent shall not be responsible for any loss or delay of documents during the mailing process.

8. All bids shall be submitted to the address specified in this Invitation for Bids no later than 08:30 on August 20, 2026 (Beijing Time). Late bids will be rejected. procnotices.project_name: Support to the Strengthening of Social Safety Nets for Human Development in Morocco Project
procnotices.bid_description: Assistance technique en expertise digitale pour la digitalisation des programmes sociaux pour le compte l’Agence Nationale du Soutien Social pour l'année 2026
procnotices.contact_address: âtiment Millennium Business Center, 3 angle avenue Mehdi Ben Barka, Souissi,Rabat-Maroc
procnotices.notice_text:
Avis à manifestation d'intérêt 

Assistance technique en expertise digitale pour la digitalisation des programmes sociaux pour le compte l’Agence Nationale du Soutien Social pour l'année 2026

Projet

Projet d’appui au renforcement des filets sociaux pour le développement humain au Maroc

Numéro du Projet

P507373

Financement

Banque mondiale

Référence STEP

MA-ANSS-560993-CS-CQS

Méthode de passation

Sélection fondée sur les qualifications des consultants (SQC/CQS)

Maître d’ouvrage

Agence Nationale du Soutien Social — ANSS

1. Objet et aperçu de la mission

Le Royaume du Maroc a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour financer le projet d’appui au renforcement des filets sociaux pour le développement humain au Maroc dont l’objectif est de renforcer l’efficacité du système de protection sociale au Maroc. Dans ce contexte l’ANSS lance cet appel à manifestation pour l’assistance technique en expertise digitale pour la digitalisation des programmes sociaux pour le compte de l’Agence Nationale du Soutien Social (ANSS) pour l’année 2026.

La prestation consiste à appuyer les équipes de l’ANSS dans la conception, le développement, l’intégration, le déploiement, la sécurisation et l’amélioration continue des solutions numériques dédiées aux programmes sociaux, à travers la mise à disposition de ressources mobilisés en présentiel sur les sites de l’ANSS, selon les besoins de l’Agence et au moyen de lettres de commande. Le volume estimatif total est de 594 jours-homme, réparti par profil et non transférable d’un profil à l’autre

Les profils à mobiliser dans le cadre de cette mission sont :  

N°

Profil à mobiliser

1

10

 

L’ANSS invite les sociétés de services éligibles à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits dans les termes de référence disponibles au téléchargement au niveau du site web de l’agence : https://anss.gov.ma/fr/appels-offres. Les sociétés intéressées doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications et l’expérience pertinente requises.

À ce stade, aucune proposition technique détaillée, aucune offre financière et aucun CV individuel d’expert ne sont demandés ni évalués. La sélection porte sur les qualifications et l’expérience du cabinet ou du groupement.

2. Consultants admis et règles applicables

Peuvent manifester leur intérêt les sociétés légalement constitués et habilités à fournir les services de développement des logiciels et l’assistance technique dans le domaine de l’IT au Maroc.

  • La société doit signaler toute situation réelle, potentielle ou apparente de conflit d’intérêts. Il ne peut être engagé pour une mission incompatible avec des obligations présentes ou passées envers d’autres clients.
  • La société sera sélectionnée selon la méthode de sélection fondée sur les qualifications des consultants (SQC/CQS), conformément au Règlement de passation des marchés de la Banque mondiale pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement.
  • L’attention des soumissionnaires est attirée sur les dispositions relatives aux conflits d’intérêts, à l’avantage concurrentiel indu et à l’éligibilité prévues notamment aux paragraphes 3.15 à 3.23 dudit Règlement. Les sociétés faisant l’objet d’une sanction en vigueur de la Banque mondiale ne sont pas éligibles.

3. Obtention des TDR et demandes d’éclaircissements

Les Termes de référence (TDR) complets ainsi que les annexes sont téléchargeables sur le site internet de l’ANSS à l’adresse suivante : https://anss.gov.ma/fr/appels-offres.

Les demandes d’éclaircissements doivent être adressées par écrit à marches@anss.ma, au plus tard le 21 août 2026, en indiquant en objet la référence MA-ANSS-560993-CS-CQS. Les réponses aux demandes d’éclaircissements ainsi que les éventuels additifs seront publiés au plus tard le 25 août 2026 sur le même lien de téléchargement du dossier de consultation : https://anss.gov.ma/fr/appels-offres. Ils feront partie intégrante du dossier de consultation.

4. Composition du dossier de la soumission

Le dossier de la manifestation d’intérêt doit comprendre :

  1. Lettre de manifestation d’intérêt cacheté et signée par une personne habilitée établie selon l’ Annexe 1 ;
  2. La ou les pièces justifiant les pouvoirs conférés à la personne agissant au nom du concurrent ;
  3. Déclaration d’acceptation des directives de la Banque Mondiale en matière de lutte contre la corruption, et de son régime de sanctions signés et cacheté (Annexe 2) ;
  4. Attestations de référence portant sur des prestations similaires à l’objet du présent avis de manifestation ou leurs copies certifiées conformes à l’original délivrées par les maîtres d’ouvrage publics ou privés, ou par les hommes de l'art sous la direction desquels le concurrent a exécuté des prestations dans le domaine de mise à disposition d'experts IT ; assistance technique IT ; développement d'applications.
  • Il est impératif que ces attestations concernent des projets réalisés au cours des cinq dernières années et portent sur des prestations avec un montant total supérieur à cinq cent mille dirhams toutes taxes comprises (500 000 DH TTC).
  1. Une attestation ou sa copie certifiée conforme à l’original, délivrée depuis moins d’un an par le percepteur du lieu d’imposition certifiant que le concurrent est en situation fiscale régulière ou à défaut de paiement qu’il a constitué les garanties. Cette attestation doit mentionner l’activité au titre de laquelle le concurrent est imposé ;
  2. Une attestation ou sa copie certifiée conforme à l’original délivrée depuis moins d’un an par la Caisse nationale de sécurité sociale ou par tout autre organisme de prévoyance sociale certifiant que le concurrent est en situation régulière envers l’organisme concerné ;

 5. Critères de sélection

Les manifestations d’intérêt reçus seront évaluées et classées sur 100 points selon les critères suivants :

Critère d'évaluation

Exigences

Notation

Pièces justificatives à fournir

A. Expérience générale du cabinet

20 points

Justifier d'au moins cinq (5) années d'expérience dans le développement logiciel et/ou l'assistance technique IT.

Expérience ≥ 5 ans : 20 points.

Expérience < 5 ans : 0 point.

Registre de commerce indiquant la date de création et l’activité

B. Expériences similaires

50 points

Références réalisées au cours des cinq (5) années précédant la date limite de remise des manifestations d'intérêt, portant sur un ou plusieurs des domaines suivants : mise à disposition d'experts IT ; assistance technique IT ; développement d'applications.

10 points par référence conforme, dans la limite de cinq (5) références.

Plafond: 50 points.

Attestations de bonne exécution ou attestations de référence délivrées par les maîtres d'ouvrage, indiquant notamment l'objet, le montant et la période d'exécution.

C. Expérience dans le secteur public

30 points

Références réalisées au profit d'administrations publiques ou d'établissements publics.

10 points par référence conforme, dans la limite de trois (3) références.

Plafond : 30 points.

Attestations de bonne exécution, ou attestations de référence délivrée par les institutions publiques (administrations, établissements …) concernées, indiquant notamment l'objet, le montant et la période d'exécution.

TOTAL

100 points

 

 

  • Il est impératif que ces attestations concernent des projets réalisés au cours des cinq dernières années et portent sur des prestations avec un montant total supérieur à cinq cent mille dirhams toutes taxes comprises (500 000 DH TTC).
  • Une même référence peut être prise en compte au titre des critères B et C lorsqu'elle porte sur une prestation similaire et qu'elle a été réalisée au profit d'une institution publique (administrations, établissements …)
  •   En cas d'égalité du score total, le cabinet ayant obtenu la meilleure note au critère B « Expériences similaires » sera classé en priorité. Si l'égalité persiste, la note obtenue au critère C sera prise en considération, en cas d’égalité toujours, un tirage au sort déterminera le classement.
  • La société ayant obtenu la meilleure note sera invitée à remettre une proposition technique et financière en vue de la négociation du contrat.

6. Présentation et dépôt des manifestations d’intérêt

La manifestation d’intérêt, rédigée en français et signée par une personne dûment habilitée, doit comprendre les pièces indiquées dans la section 4 « Composition du dossier de la soumission » ci-après.

Elle doit être reçue au plus tard le  31 août 2026 à 10h00. L’ouverture des manifestations d’intérêt est prévue le même jour à 10h00. Les dossiers peuvent être transmis selon l’un des modes suivants :

  • Dépôt physique ou par voie postale : sous pli fermé adressé au Service Marchés de l’ANSS, bâtiment Millennium Business Center, 3 angle avenue Mehdi Ben Barka, Souissi, Rabat. Le dossier est présenté en un (1) exemplaire original, accompagné d’une version électronique sur support numérique.
  • Transmission électronique : à l’adresse marches@anss.ma. Tous les documents constituant la manifestation d’intérêt doivent être transmis en format PDF , signés électroniquement et  être lisibles.

Le pli ou l’objet du courriel doit porter la mention : « Manifestation d’intérêt – MA-ANSS-560993-CS-CQS – Expertise digitale – Ne pas ouvrir avant le 31 août 2026 à 10h00 ».
